#75553. New electric comb from China regrew nearly 100% of hair (in mice)

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (800 w)
📖 Baca
EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Popsci ↗ Open Full Page

New electric comb from China regrew nearly 100% of hair (in mice)

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (800 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Popsci

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, A potentially revolutionary electronic comb is generating some pretty hair-raising results.
  • Though the Detangle comb (named after the 2010 Disney film Tangled) hasn’t been tested on humans yet, the Chinese scientist behind its development says the eye-grabbing results on our distant genetic cousins suggest it could play a role in the neverending quest to keep those luscious locks just a hair longer.
  • Sources indicate that created by a team led by Beihang University in Beijing, the comb initially looks like the chunky plastic kind adorning typical pharmacy aisles.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, A potentially revolutionary electronic comb is generating some pretty hair-raising results. The experimental comb has been used to successfully restore nearly all the hair in bald test subjects. But don’t chuck out that Rogaine just yet. The comb’s people were mice with shaved backs.

Though the Detangle comb (named after the 2010 Disney film Tangled) hasn’t been tested on humans yet, the Chinese scientist behind its development says the eye-grabbing results on our distant genetic cousins suggest it could play a role in the neverending quest to keep those luscious locks just a hair longer.

Sources indicate that created by a team led by Beihang University in Beijing, the comb initially looks like the chunky plastic kind adorning typical pharmacy aisles. However, a closer look at its clear plastic handle reveals a green circuit board. Further down, one can see electrodes embedded in the comb’s teeth, which alternate between long and short. The team notes that this height variance makes the comb’s pulsed electric field more than two and a half times stronger than it would be with evenly matched teeth.

It has been revealed that the shorter teeth also contain two experimental genetic treatments. One boosts blood vessel growth around the hair follicles. The other treatment  blocks dihydrotestosterone (DHT), a hormone known to shrink follicles. The electric field generated by the comb temporarily opens up skin so the treatments can get inside, reaching up to nine times deeper into the follicle region than a conventional cream.​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​.

Researchers performed a variety of tests on mice that had their backs shaved and were given testosterone to mimic pattern baldness. Over 28 days, the balding mice were treated with minoxidil or finasteride (the current standards for medical hair restoration), the comb’s electrical stimulation alone, and the comb combined with an experimental genetic treatment. Mice given finasteride regrew about 50 percent of their hair, while the ones on and minoxidil regrew 70 percent. Those numbers  honestly aren’t  too bad on their own, but the results were even better when Detangle got involved. Mice treated with the comb and both experimental treatments saw a staggering 97.85 percent hair regrowth. And all without having to book a flight to Turkey for a hair transplant.

“[T]hese results demonstrate that electrostimulation via the Detangle system promotes hair growth and follicle regeneration in a safe and effective manner,” the team wrote in their paper published earlier this month in the Nature Communications.

Sources indicate that the potential market for a hair regrowing comb is sizable to say the least. Detangle’’s creators say androgenetic alopecia, the scientific term for pattern baldness, affects 1.5 billion people worldwide. Some studies suggest up to 80 percent of men will experience pattern baldness, with  some populations seeing symptoms before the age of 40. Somewhere between one fifth and two fifths of women may also experience pattern hair thinning. And hair isn’t just hair. Social expectations and norms around hair partly explain why hair loss can carry psychological baggage.

Scientists and hair care providers know this, of course. Toupees, tonics, and tinctures promising to reverse nature’s balding date back thousands of years. Today, the standard medical treatment usually involves topical minoxidil (the active ingredient in Rogaine) and oral finasteride. Minoxidil generally works, but results vary widely from person to person and it requires constant, ongoing application.

According to recent reports, finasteride is often far more effective, with long-term studies showing it can preserve hair in most men for at least a decade, but it also carries the risk for much more intense side effects. The drug (which saw a surge in popularity thanks to online, telehealth services) has been linked to decreased libido and erectile dysfunction. Some patients have also reported anxiety, depression, and suicidal thoughts. While the side effects are uncommon, the risk presented a potentially steep trade off for a fuller head of hair.

It has been revealed that those intrigued by the comb will unfortunately have to hold out quite a bit longer. The team claims more research is needed before the device is tested on humans and, even then, there’s no guarantee the rodent results will translate. Testosterone-induced hair loss on a shaved mouse back is a far cry from human pattern baldness, which typically creeps in over years.

It’s also worth emphasizing that the electric comb, memorable as it is, wasn’t solely responsible for the best results. The pair of experimental genetic treatments used in the study (called SRD5A2 siRNA and VEGFA plasmids) also need to be tested in humans to ensure they are safe and don’t come with unintended side effects of their own. Wig stores, it seems, will live to see another day.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • A 2024 study published in JAMA Ophthalmology “initially triggered” the FDA’s review, the agency told Healthline.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GLP-1 consumers have a new symptom to watch for: Sudden vision loss in one eye.

The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) announced on November 9 that it will require drugmakers to add information to the warning labels of Ozempic, Wegovy, Mounjaro, Zepbound and other GLP-1 medications about “a potential increased risk” of a rare eye condition called nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION).GLP-1 medications are approved to treat type 2 diabetes and to help people lose weight and keep it off.NAION joins a growing list of side effects linked to GLP-1s, adding a second eye warning to several labels.The U.S. labels for Ozempic, Rybelsus, Trulicity, Mounjaro, and Zepbound already warn about diabetic retinopathy, a diabetes-related eye disease, according to each drug’s prescribing information.The two conditions affect different parts of the eye. Diabetic retinopathy damages tiny blood vessels in the retina, the layer at the back of the eye that senses light, according to the National Eye Institute. NAION damages the optic nerve when it doesn’t get enough blood, according to the FDA’s announcement.Mihail Zilbermint, MD, director of endocrine hospitalists at Johns Hopkins, told Healthline he hasn’t seen NAION in his patients. He has seen vision worsen in some people after they start a GLP-1.“But we believe that’s probably related to rapid improvement in their sugar control, which can also be seen in someone who is starting insulin,” Zilbermint said.

A 2024 study published in JAMA Ophthalmology “initially triggered” the FDA’s review, the agency told Healthline.

Sources indicate that the study found a higher risk of NAION in people prescribed semaglutide, the active ingredient in Ozempic and Wegovy, than in people prescribed other diabetes or weight-loss drugs.The authors wrote that more research is needed to determine whether semaglutide causes NAION.Joseph F. Rizzo III, MD, director of the Neuro-Ophthalmology Service at Mass Eye and Ear in Boston, served as the study’s corresponding author.

Sources indicate that in a 2024 podcast, Rizzo said he and a resident saw three patients with NAION who were taking semaglutide for about a week.“And because NAION is a fairly uncommon disorder in the general population, the fact that we had three within a relatively short period of time led me to suspect that there was a higher risk of developing NAION in patients on semaglutide,” Rizzo said. The FDA analyzed clinical trials for multiple GLP-1 drugs and noted that NAION cases were reported with every GLP-1 on the market, according to its announcement. Those findings led the FDA to require the warning for the entire drug class, the agency told Healthline.

It has been revealed that about 70% to 80% of people with NAION first notice vision loss when they wake up, according to StatPearls. The FDA listed these symptoms:.

No treatment has been proven to reverse vision loss from NAION, according to StatPearls.

“Patients experiencing sudden, painless vision loss in one eye should contact their healthcare professional immediately and should not stop their medication without consulting their provider first,” the FDA told Healthline.

In the announcement, the agency told doctors to promptly refer patients with suspected NAION to an ophthalmologist.

The FDA listed these possible risk factors for NAION:.

The FDA told Healthline that many people who take GLP-1s also have these conditions, which made reports of NAION in GLP-1 users “challenging” to interpret.

In a recent development, across 126 clinical trials, the FDA found about 6 NAION cases per 100,000 people taking a GLP-1 for a year, and about 4 per 100,000 people taking a placebo or another diabetes drug for a year.In real-world data, NAION was more common with GLP-1s than with one type of diabetes pill, but the FDA found no significant increase compared with another type, the agency told Healthline.Zilbermint said patients who saw the news have worried about losing their vision. He tells them that “many of the serious harms, including the potential harm of NAION, are rare.”“The overall risk is still very small,” he said.

Regulators in other countries have added NAION warnings, mostly for semaglutide:.

The FDA told Healthline the benefits of GLP-1s “continue to outweigh their risks when used as directed.”The FDA has also approved some GLP-1s to lower the risk of heart attack and stroke, reduce the risk of worsening kidney disease, and treat sleep apnea and a type of liver disease.Zilbermint noted that “for most of my patients with obesity, diabetes and heart disease, the benefits clearly outweigh the risks.”“But we definitely have to decide patient by patient,” he added.

The labeling change applies to these medications, according to the FDA’s announcement:.

As of publication, the FDA’s online label database did not yet show the new warning on the drugs’ labels.

#75551. Industry News: Why You May Need an "Elevator Message" About Healthy Aging

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (883 w)

Industry News: Why You May Need an "Elevator Message" About Healthy Aging

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (883 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Posted November 20, 2026 | Reviewed by Tyler Woods.
  • “Of all the self-fulfilling prophecies in our culture the assumption that aging means decline and poor health is probably the deadliest.” --Marilyn Ferguson, author.
  • I was in an elevator with two preschool children in Halloween costumes, their parents, and an older couple.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 20, 2026 | Reviewed by Tyler Woods.

“Of all the self-fulfilling prophecies in our culture the assumption that aging means decline and poor health is probably the deadliest.” --Marilyn Ferguson, author.

I was in an elevator with two preschool children in Halloween costumes, their parents, and an older couple.

The older man commented to the smiling children, “Oh, you are going to have fun on Halloween, I see.” The children and parents nodded at him in the affirmative.

Then he sighed and noted, “When you’re my age, you have a lot of aches and pains. Life is not as much fun when you get older.”.

I was taken aback. So many negative stereotypes about aging in two short sentences, including the classic myth that old age is an inevitable process of decline and deterioration. I responded, “I don’t agree. I’m 82, and I’m enjoying life more than ever.”.

Sources indicate that the man said, “Well, I’m 73. You look very young for your age.” Was he implying that I was the exception that proved the rule?

I’m not above fishing for compliments, but in this case, I was after something more notable—sending positive messages about aging to young children. I never realized I was going to need an “elevator message” to do it.

Recent findings suggest that usually, an “elevator message” refers to a business networking tool, consisting of one or two short sentences about who you are, what you do, and how your skills could benefit the listener, according to speaking coach Fred Miller. The idea of an elevator message is to convey the most key things about you during a short elevator ride. "Elevator messages" don't need to take place in actual elevators, of course. These messages can be employed at conferences, book signings, or even in the line at the coffee house. Writers, for example, can describe their background and latest book project; job-seekers can tout their most important accomplishments.

I had never previously considered that I might someday need an elevator message to combat stereotypes about aging. What I said was simply a gut reaction to the situation. And the reason I am still mulling over what I said, and what I could have said, is because there was a life-and-death situation at stake. Well, not exactly, but here’s the research.

In a recent development, psychology professor Becca Levy has researched the health and longevity effects of age beliefs. In one study, published in 2002, she and her colleagues followed 660 adults 50 and older and discovered that participants with a positive view of aging lived on average 7.5 years longer than participants with a negative view of aging.

It has been revealed that in her 2022 book, Breaking the Age Code, Levy cites other studies showing that people who held positive age beliefs scored 30% better on memory tests than those with negative age beliefs. She has also discovered that age stereotypes affect a surprising number of areas—for example, those with negative age beliefs had a slower gait, lower self-esteem, and exercised less. (For more details, check out this blog on how positive age beliefs can reduce dementia risk.).

According to recent reports, add to these results the amazing finding that most older people are happier people, as shown by numerous surveys. I was so shocked to learn the relationship between aging and happiness that I wrote a whole book (Silver Sparks) and numerous blogs about it. In addition, older people have good mental health, including a positive outlook on life. As researcher Laura Carstensen states: “People over the age of 65 have the most stable and optimistic outlook of all adults.”.

According to recent reports, of course, one negative comment in an elevator would be unlikely to mold the mentality of those young children. But I would suspect that a drumbeat of negative, ageist comments like the one I overheard could eventually have an effect on the mental outlook of those who hear them…which is everybody.

Sources indicate that young children and young adults are not the only ones who could benefit from an age-positive elevator message. A thoughtful message might also remind older people to challenge their own internalized ageism and recall the benefits of getting older.

Can we construct pithy elevator messages to replace the knee-jerk comments about ageism?

To jog your brain, consider these elevator messages about aging that are positive and accurate:.

What we say to children about aging will, of course, depend upon the age of the child and the situation.

With better messages about aging, we can help children face their future with optimism, possibly affecting their lifespan, healthspan, and mental health. And by voicing the positive truths about aging, we could also remind ourselves of the many advantages of growing older.

Here’s a challenge for you: What’s your idea for an elevator message about the benefits of growing older?

Thanks to my 11-year-old granddaughter Eloise for her ideas about elevator messages.

It’s pretty clear at this stage that Arc Raiders is one of the biggest launches of 2025. More interesting than the numbers themselves, however, is that this is an extraction shooter - a subgenre which has typically been thought of as niche.

If you’ve been paying the PvPvE game any attention, you could easily see how (and why) it keeps breaking its own records.

Recent findings suggest that today, publisher Nexon declared in a press release (via Gematsu) that Arc Raiders has now sold over 4 million copies. The game came out on October 30, which means it managed to sell that many copies in a little over 10 days.

The news comes on the same day that developer Embark Studios revealed that the game had more than 700,000 concurrent players across all platforms over the weekend. Over the same weekend on Steam alone, Arc Raiders broke its own Steam concurrent record with a newly introduced peak of 462,488 players - which is a significant chunk of that 700,000+ player base.

Sources indicate that this marks the second time the extraction shooter has broken its own concurrent player records, which is something very few games have managed in the past. Arc Raiders remains a top-seller, too. On Steam, it’s currently the second-best seller globally (by revenue), sitting just below Counter-Strike 2.

“The many different ways you play and participate in ARC Raiders have completely blown us away, going far beyond what we ever imagined. You surprise us, you outsmart us, and you keep us on our toes. We wouldn’t have it any other way,” the developer wrote on Twitter.

Embark recently published a roadmap to highlight all the new content coming to the game over the remainder of this year. The first new map is set to arrive this month alongside new Arc units, new gameplay items, new events and more.

Just over the weekend, the game received several upcoming Map Conditions that completely alter the way they play. The developer has already rolled out a couple of updates since launch, in order to tackle exploits and fix a few launchday bugs.

It has been revealed that if you’re right now hooked on this gem of a game, we guarantee that our Arc Raiders gameplay tips will have at least one you didn’t know about. We also have more guides on how to find some of the more elusive items in the game, such as olives, lemons and apricots, and prickly pears.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Amflow has made a name for itself in the electric mountain bike world with its high-performance Avinox-powered machines, but now the company is bringing that same technology to a decidedly more urban environment. The newly unveiled Amflow UE Carbon series marks the brand’s first move into the commuter e-bike market, combining a lightweight carbon fiber frame, powerful mid-drive motor, and a surprisingly long list of smart features designed for everyday riding.

And while these might look like fairly conventional step-through city bikes at first glance, there’s some seriously impressive technology hiding beneath those clean lines.

The new Amflow UE series comes in two versions, the UE Carbon and the higher-end UE Carbon Pro, both built around a full-carbon fiber frame weighing just 2.35 kg (5.2 lb).

The complete bike weighs as little as 20.9 kg (46 lb), which is fairly impressive considering the amount of hardware Amflow has packed into it, including front suspension, a suspension dropper seatpost, integrated lighting, and cargo racks.

Recent findings suggest that both models use the Avinox M2 mid-drive motor, which delivers up to 125 Nm of torque. That’s an enormous amount of torque for a city bike, and should make short work of steep hills, especially when carrying groceries or other cargo. And to put things into perspective, a lot of city e-bikes have barely 60 Nm for torque, so Amflow is knocking it out of the park for urban power.

A removable 600 Wh battery provides a claimed maximum range of 132 km (82 miles) in the lowest power assist mode, while fast charging can refill the battery in just 2 hours and 23 minutes.

The bikes also feature Avinox’s intelligent traction control system and a newly introduced Auto Boost function that automatically provides additional assistance when the system detects demanding conditions, such as accelerating from a stop or climbing a steep hill.

In other words, riders get much of the sophisticated motor technology developed for high-performance electric mountain bikes, but in a package designed for commuting to work or picking up groceries.

The bike is listed as weighing 20.9 kg (46 lb), though that figure conveniently excludes the front and rear racks, mudguards, pedals, kickstand, bike lock, bottle cage, and chainguard. So figure a few extra pounds for all of that gear, and you’re in the right ballpark.

The main difference between the two models is their drivetrain.

The higher-end UE Carbon Pro ($3,899) uses a customized three-speed electronically shifted internally geared hub paired with a Gates carbon belt drive. That should make it particularly appealing to commuters who want a quiet, clean, low-maintenance setup without worrying about chain lubrication or derailleur adjustments.

The more affordable UE Carbon ($3,499) instead uses a 10-speed electronic derailleur developed with TRP.

Both models support automatic shifting, allowing the bike to handle gear changes without requiring the rider to constantly think about them.

Amflow has also gone fairly wild with the technology integration.

There’s a 1.4-inch touchscreen display mounted on the handlebars, a wireless phone charging mount offering 15W wireless charging or 20W USB-C charging, and integrated lighting with automatic low-light activation and brake-sensing functionality.

The bikes even include a hardened steel frame lock on the rear wheel, Apple Find My integration, and a Lost Mode feature that can lock down certain components if the bike is stolen.

Apple Watch connectivity allows riders to check their bike’s status and unlock it, while heart-rate-based assistance can automatically adjust motor output to help riders maintain a target heart rate zone.

Some of these features, like the security and tracking, are immediately effective for nearly all riders, while other high-tech features like the heart rate-based pedal assist can provide even more functionality for niche riders looking to bridge the gap between riding for transportation and riding for fitness.

Of course, all the fancy technology in the world doesn’t mean much if a commuter bike can’t handle everyday errands.

Fortunately, Amflow appears to have taken the practical side seriously.

The bikes feature a low step-through frame, upright riding position, 65 mm suspension fork, and a suspension dropper seatpost offering 125 mm of height adjustment and approximately 30 mm of suspension travel.

The 26×2.0-inch Maxxis tires should also provide a comfortable ride over less-than-perfect city streets.

There’s a front rack rated for 20 kg (44 lb) and a rear rack rated for 27 kg (59.5 lb), with the latter supporting the MIK HD mounting system for compatible accessories, including child seats.

The standard frame is designed to accommodate riders from 155 to 190 cm (5’1” to 6’3”), while a smaller version for riders down to 140 cm (4’7”) is expected in 2027.

I’ve been impressed with the technology coming out of the Avinox ecosystem, and it’s exciting to see that technology finally make its way into a more practical city-focused electric bicycle.

As much as I love high-performance electric mountain bikes, the reality is that most people aren’t spending their mornings bombing down mountain trails. They’re commuting to work, dropping kids off at school, and running errands.

And that’s where electric bicycles can make an even bigger difference.

The Amflow UE series seems to take a refreshingly comprehensive approach to urban riding. The powerful motor is nice, but I’m arguably more interested in the belt drive, integrated security, cargo capacity, automatic shifting, and built-in phone charging.

Industry observers note that those are the kinds of features that can make an electric bicycle genuinely easier to live with every day. And as someone who actually commutes with an e-bike each day as my main form of transportation, these bikes are really speaking to me!

According to recent reports, if you ask me, it’s great to see another high-performance e-bike manufacturer recognizing that the future of electric bicycles isn’t just about riding farther and faster on trails. It’s also about making everyday transportation better for the less exciting type of riding, too.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • “We are in shock at the moment,” Cincinnati Zoo director Dave Jenike said in a statement.
  • Recent findings suggest that last week, a child’s knit hat entered her enclosure at the Cincinnati Zoo and the almost 10-year-old hippo ate it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Cincinnati Zoo’s most famous resident Fiona the hippo has died at age 9.

“We are in shock at the moment,” Cincinnati Zoo director Dave Jenike said in a statement. “We did not expect this outcome. She fought until she couldn’t anymore. Our animal care team was heroic in their efforts to save her. They did everything possible, but her body couldn’t fight anymore. She was dearly loved by her Zoo family and countless others around the world. Her loss will be felt deeply by so many.”.

Recent findings suggest that last week, a child’s knit hat entered her enclosure at the Cincinnati Zoo and the almost 10-year-old hippo ate it. Given her size, zookeepers initially thought she’d simply pass the hat, but it remained stuck in her digestive track. She had undergone a colonoscopy using a 9-foot scope and multiple ultrasounds that indicated intestinal bunching, indicating her body was trying and expel the hat. Caretakers have continued to give her fluids and sedate her when necessary for tests. Just yesterday, on November 18, the zoo shared a fresh approach in Fiona’s ongoing treatment: a vibration plate borrowed from a local Ohio horse farm. Fiona could be seen standing on the plate, vocalizing to caretakers.

It has been revealed that “Fiona was such a gift,” mentioned Cincinnati Zoo Executive Chair of the Board Thane Maynard. “I have never known an animal so beloved in all my life. From the day she was born, she was like lightning in a bottle. And, she will be remembered and beloved many years from now.”.

Fiona first captured the internet’s heart in 2017, when she was born six weeks premature. Baby hippos typically weigh about 100 pounds at birth, but tiny Fiona tipped the scales at a mere 29 pounds. She was the smallest known hippo to survive such a low birth weight. As she grew, Fiona took social media and the real world by storm: she photobombed an engagement shoot, had a local ice cream named in her honor, and even starred in her own reality-TV series appropriately called “The Fiona Show.”  Her surprise baby brother Fritz was born in 2022, after their mother’s birth control went “on the fritz.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, if your domicile happens to exist, say, under a large boulder, you might not have heard that Grand Theft Auto VI is finally arriving at the stroke of midnight on November 19. Those of us who watch television, browse the web, scroll social media, listen to the radio, read the newspaper, flip through magazines, or consume outside info in any way are well aware of the video game, however. It’s the latest installment of the immensely popular “Grand Theft Auto” series, which combines a (surprisingly deep) vein of car culture with an immersive open world full of theft, fighting, drugs, and other violent delights.

While the previous games came out on a semi-regular schedule of one every few years, it’s been 13 trips ‘round the sun since the last one hit stores. (GTA VI’s development has been so delayed, it even inspired a meme.) Suffice it to say, there’s a lot of pent-up anticipation—even enough to spark half-founded panic headlines about millions of people around the world call in sick to play. But there’s another report that puts a bit more solid of a figure on the excitement around the game. According to digital analysis firm SensorTower, GTA VI has already racked up $1.65 billion in pre-sales ahead of its launch.

That correlates to a little over 17 million orders for the game so far, according to the report, with 75 percent of pre-sales going for the PlayStation 5 version and the other 25 percent for Xbox Series X|S consoles. The chart indicates a fairly typical exponential curve growth over the last five months since pre-sales kicked off: a long period of incremental gains, followed by rapid acceleration in the last few weeks.

And GTA VI-based revenue seems likely to keep coming in to creator Rockstar Games’s coffers at quite a clip, considering initial reviews for the game have been stellar so far. While it may not be your typical automotive-themed driving game, the latest release seems all but sure to guarantee Grand Theft Auto remains a serious part of car culture for some time to come.

Will Sabel Courtney is a contributing editor at Road & Track. A 12-year veteran of journalism, he formerly worked at Gear Patrol, The Drive, and RIDES Magazine, and contributed to the New York Daily News and Jalopnik, among other outlets. You can often find him test-driving new cars in New York City, cursing the slow-moving traffic surrounding him.

The 61 Best Latest Shows of 2026 (and 1 More We Can't Wait For)

📅 13 Feb 2026 | ⏱️ 12 min read (2376 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Menshealth

⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • THE IDEA OF "new" television demonstrates is a little bit of a tricky one these days.
  • Sources indicate that but at the same time, they aren't entirely wrong.
  • Look, we can't beat too much around the bush: People love nostalgia, people love things they recognize and remember, and it can be pretty hard to get anyone to even attempt to give their attention to something new, let alone get really into it in the way we all like to with the very best of TV.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

THE IDEA OF "new" television demonstrates is a little bit of a tricky one these days. Sure, we do still get a fair share of truly new, exciting, unique ideas each year—just look at shows like Severance a couple years ago and Pluribus last year. Shows like last year's The Lowdown—rich, well-written, character-focused stories—still draw major stars like Ethan Hawke and still hit in a major way for audiences that watch it. If someone was being dramatic and wanted to say original TV was dead, dying, or on life support, there's plenty of evidence out there to throw in their face.

Sources indicate that but at the same time, they aren't entirely wrong. For one reason or another, so much of the TV landscape—even shows we're really excited for—are based around something that in one way or another already exists.

Look, we can't beat too much around the bush: People love nostalgia, people love things they recognize and remember, and it can be pretty hard to get anyone to even attempt to give their attention to something new, let alone get really into it in the way we all like to with the very best of TV. Which is why we kind of have two different options here—people need to be really trusting of word of mouth and really aware when something is a really good new, original show (because no one likes to waste their time with a piece of junk), and we just need to really hope that all the remakes, reboots, reimaginings, and re-whatevers are good.

In a recent development, and they should be! HBO's Lanterns is modeled after True Detective, stars Kyle Chandler and Aaron Pierre as the titular Green Lanterns, and counts Watchmen genius Damon Lindelof as a producer. Of course it’s good. Below, we're going to keep track all year. We're charting the indicates we already know are good. We're charting the shows we think might be good. And we're charting the shows that may not even come out this year, but if they do... they still might not be good. But, again, say it with us: We're choosing to be hopeful.

Netflix has been really good of late at the pulpy, potboiler, limited series, and His & Hers is the latest in that winning streak. The show follows a detective (Jon Bernthal) and his estranged journalist wife (Tessa Thompson) as they both hunt for answers when a local woman—whom they both have a close connection to—winds up dead. Based on Alice Feeney's book of the same name, His & Hers is exactly how this kind of show should be: Juicy, fun, easy to watch, and filled with really good actors.

A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms (HBO).

In a recent development, in shrinking its story down to a more intimate one that takes place between the margins of major universe events, Game of Thrones takes a page out of the Andor handbook with A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms (based on George R.R. Martin's Dunk and Egg novellas). This short series, which follows a big, humble, anxious hedge knight (former professional rugby playerPeter Claffey)and his little friend/squire (Dexter Sol Ansell) is a true breath of fresh air for Thrones fans on both a story and character level. It's a delight.

Doesn't the premise of Ponies just sound fun? This spy series set in '70s Moscow follows a pair of women working with the CIA who find themselves at the midst of a vast conspiracy when their husbands both die under mysterious circumstances. And those women are played by The White Lotus's Haley Lu Richardson and Game of Thrones queen Emilia Clarke. Sometimes something that sounds like a winner just turns out to be one.

The Fall and Rise of Reggie Dinkins (NBC/Peacock).

Recent findings suggest that this show about a disgraced former football player (Tracy Morgan) and a documentary filmmaker following him (Daniel Radcliffe) comes from the team behind 30 Rock, so you know you're going to get several jokes per minute. Plus, Morgan and Radcliffe are no slouches themselves. The show had a special debut in January and will continue on a regular schedule later in February.

According to recent reports, at the very least, Wonder Man is among the best shows Marvel ever made—and you could make a case that it's at the top of the list. Yahya Abdul Mateen II plays the titular hero (aka actor Simon Williams) as the kind of guy we love to love in this sort of story: humble, well-meaning, charismatic, and ambitious. But when he meets fellow actor (and former fake terrorist) Trevor Slattery (Ben Kingsley) and learns that his favorite movie from childhood is being remade by an acclaimed director, everything changes. Wonder Man isn't just a good Marvel show, but a good show about people, movies, and friendship period. Let's hope the MCU takes notes from what worked so well here and keeps the streak going in the future.

One of America's great cultural institutions made its grand return in 2026: The Muppet Show! This version—coming from executive producers Seth Rogen and Evan Goldberg—is directly modeled on the original Muppet Show, which means special guests, musical performances, comedy sketches, and lots of fun. The first episode, which featured special guest star Sabrina Carpenter, was an absolute delight for anyone who likes Kermit, Miss Piggy, and friends (or who just likes laughing and having a good time). For now, it's just this one episode, but if the reaction is strong enough (and it seems like it might be), the show will come back in full.

Sources indicate that the latest entry in producer Ryan Murphy's American Story universe is called Love Story, and follows the romance and life between Carolyn Bessette Kennedy and John F. Kennedy Jr. The show is, however, much better than that tabloid-y description sounds; Sarah Pidgeon, who plays Carolyn, is a star, coming off her Tony-nominated role in the Fleetwood Mac-inspired play Stereophonic. But Paul Anthony Kelly, who plays JFK Jr., is a real discovery—it's his first role (he was previously a model), and he truly feels like a reincarnation of the late attorney/magazine publisher/dashing public figure. Of course, this is a story that ends in an extreme tragedy—so if you get invested, be sure to have your tissues ready.

Industry observers note that this wild documentary series looks at different disputes between neighbors, telling compelling and often escalating true stories that will truly floor you in the depiction of their very-real truth. Think about this less as a story about the legalities of these disputes, and more a look into some larger-than-life characters through an often trippy, absurd lens. The series is produced by Josh Safdie and Ronald Bronstein, coming off of their recent success on the Oscar-nominated Marty Supreme.

It has been revealed that the latest season of Scrubs brings back almost all of the original cast, including Zach Braff, Donald Faison, and Sarah Chalke. And audiences who love and/or remember that trio and most of the show's original dramedy premise should be pleased with this new version of the beloved aughts sitcom. The last season aired in 2010, so we're OK with calling this 16-years-later revival a 'new' show.

DTF St. Louis follows trio of languishing adults—played by the electric trio of Jason Bateman, Linda Cardellini, and David Harbour—who get involved in a love triangle and general madness that results in one of them winding up dead. You may think you have an idea of what you're getting into with this show based on the cast and that premise, but believe us—all of your expectations will be upended. DTF St. Louis is a tonal balancing act, a show that bounces between hilarious dark comedy, compelling mystery, and gutting, relatable drama. It's one of the best shows of the year.

The second age of Yellowstone begins in earnest with Marshals, a 13-episode drama that airs on CBS (and streams on Parmaount+ either simultaneously or a day later, depending on which tier of subscription you have). The series focuses on Luke Grimes's character Kayce, and how an old SEAL Team leader (Logan Marshall-Green) recruits him into his Marshal squad. There's at least one more Yellowstone spinoff coming in 2026—Dutton Ranch—and so this is the one leading the charge.

Recent findings suggest that one of the busiest men in show business these days—on both the massive and small screen—is Guy Ritchie, and his newest endeavor takes him back to a world he's inhabited a couple times before. Young Sherlock follows, well, a Young Sherlock Holmes. And as you can imagine, it follows Arthur Conan Doyle's famous detective as he solves a mystery. Hero Fiennes Tiffin plays the titular character, and Colin Firth is also part of the show's cast. If you're into that, you'll have a fun time! It's an enjoyable show.

Recent findings suggest that the erotic thriller is back! Or, well, juicy erotic character study dramedy? Whatever we want to call it, Netflix's Vladimir is one of the year's most exciting upcoming shows. Based on the novel of the same name, this show follows a longtime literature professor at a college (Rachel Weisz, constantly breaking the fourth wall) who finds herself in the midst of controversy when her fellow professor husband (John Slattery) gets caught sleeping with students. She takes this as an opportunity to switch things up a bit, and so she becomes smitten with her very sexy new colleague (Leo Woodall). It's a fun, zippy, juicy time—and kind of like if Deadpool was actually about a smart woman in academia who's spinning her wheels and maybe just a little bit horny.

From the mold of Ted Lasso and Shrinking comes Rooster, which stars Steve Carell and counts Lasso and Shrinking co-creator Bill Lawrence (who also made Scrubs and Cougar Town) as its showrunner. Carell plays an author who heads to help his professor daughter on a college campus... and becomes enamored with life there. Imagine Back to School but with some middle-age soul-searching and academia at play? Sure! HBO's got another winner on their hands with this one—and maybe Carell can get the Emmy that he somehow never got for The Office.

It has been revealed that there are 29 books in the Scarpetta series, and, now, one TV show on Prime Video starring Nicole Kidman and Jamie Lee Curtis. The series follows forensic pathologist Dr. Kay Scarpetta (Kidman) as she solves a crime—but the show is so much more than just that. In a way, Scarpetta is destined to fit into Prime Video's roster of rock-solid procedural murder mysteries, which also includes Reacher, Cross, Bosch, and plenty more. But it's got a little bit of an extra chaotic oomph—helped out by the star-studded cast that also includes Bobby Cannavale and Simon Baker—that make it worth your while and a unique, fun show.

Sources indicate that sunny Nights, which aired in Australia last year, now makes its U.S. debut on Hulu. The premise is simple: A pair of siblings (played by the very funny Will Forte and D'Arcy Carden) want to start a spray tan business, but wind up entrenched in the criminal underworld. Whoops! Forte and Carden have been two of our finest comedic actors for a while—with ability to play depth in addition to that humor—and the show thrives when they're at their strongest. A solid watch for anyone looking for something light but compelling.

Sources indicate that this series—from Yellowstone super writer/producer Taylor Sheridan—follows Stacy Clyburn (Michelle Pfeiffer) and her family, as they move from the busy, stressful world of Newly introduced York City to a more rustic setting out in beautiful Montana after a totally unforseen tragedy. Kurt Russellplays her husband, Preston, with his usual endless charisma, while the supporting cast includes the likes of Matthew Fox and Suits star Patrick J. Adams. Sheridan does his usual zigging and zagging in The Madison—the tone can sometimes shift from very sad to zany and comedic, and, as usual, there's a bit of social commentary speechifying buried in almost every scene. But if you're on board with the writing style he uses in highlights like Yellowstone and Landman, you'll probably be OK with it here, especially if you're ready for a heavier and more contemplative tone. This show was originally planned to be part of the Yellowstone connected universe, but those prepares have since been changed; It's now a new story, but with that Montana setting, you still get to look at all sorts of beautiful landscapes.

Jury Duty: Organization Retreat (Prime Video).

After striking gold a couple years ago with Jury Duty, Prime Video gives its grand Truman Show-esque experiment another try with a second season called Manufacturer Retreat. This time around, we follow a regular guy who thinks he’s working as a temp for a hot sauce company and joining them on their annual company bonding retreat. Of course, everyone around him is actually an actor in a scripted, engineered situation. It’s a little goofier than the first season, but seeing how everything plays out is compelling, often very funny television nonetheless. A worthy follow-up, and, honestly, we might just watch these as long as they feel like making them.

Riz Ahmed is the creator and star of Bait, a show about an actor who thinks he's about to get offered the role of a lifetime—James Bond!—and the madness that spirals out of such a revelation. If you're a fan of Ahmed's (and why wouldn't you be?) this will be a fun ride.

Something Very Bad Is Going To Happen (Netflix).

Camila Morrone (Daisy Jones and the Six) and Adam DiMarco(The White Lotus) are set to get married in this horror series from showrunner Haley Z. Boston (who worked on the very underrated Brand Fresh Cherry Flavor) and producers The Duffer Brothers. And not to oversell, but Something Very Bad Is Going to Happen is the best horror show I've seen in quite some time. While the show plays with familiar settings and tropes—you may think of Ready or Not or Midsommar during the show's eight episodes—it's so filled with Ari Aster-esque dread and stunning, striking camera work that it doesn't even matter. Horror fans are in for an absolute treat with this one.

  • The experience and expression of human attachment is complex, to say the least.
  • Are you someone who obsesses about others?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 20, 2026 | Reviewed by Monica Vilhauer Ph.D.

The experience and expression of human attachment is complex, to say the least. As humans, we may share a universal ingrained wiring for connection, but how we navigate this interpersonal world is not the same from person to person.

Are you someone who obsesses about others? Maybe you understand infatuation in the early stages of love, but then know how to transition to a mutual relationship or let go? Forming steady and stable connections is easy for some people; others are tortured with intense and uncertain attachments. Fresh research provides insight into limerence, a specific form of intense attachment that is starting to gain more attention.

Industry observers note that imagine someone fixating on another person. This isn't hard to do. We hear about it on podcasts, watch it unfold in fantastic crime dramas, and, of course, some of us experience it in real life. From infatuation to unrequited love, examples of preoccupations with another person, outside of established relationships, color the romantic landscape. Limerence, however, is different.

Industry observers note that limerence is an intense and highly disruptive cognitive and emotional experience (Marshall et al., 2025; Tennov, 1979). Individuals in the throes of limerence are overwhelmed by the desire to be viewed positively by a specific someone else (i.e., the limerence object). This obsession manifests as uncontrollable rumination to the point that it interferes with day-to-day life.

According to recent reports, limerence is typically expressed toward someone with whom the experiencer is highly unlikely to form a real relationship. On the surface, this might seem like unrequited love, but it is far more intense and generally less realistic.

From a case study analysis, Wyant (2021) offered the following pathway by which people might come to experience limerence:.

It has been revealed that A recent review (Bradbury et al., 2025) summarized a step-wise sequence proposed by Verhulst (1984). This model suggests that limerence begins in the context of need: a person's needs for emotional intimacy, support, and connection are not fulfilled in their current relationships. Limerence can follow from there:.

Sources indicate that different dimensions of limerence are predictable by key psychological constructs. Recent research suggests limerence is best understood as a two-dimensional construct, comprised of both an intense need for attachment and neglect of self or others (Marshall et al., 2025).

It has been revealed that attachment anxiety, imaginative fantasy (i.e., the tendency to daydream), and the need to belong are linked to the need-for-attachment dimension of limerence for those experiencing it. This dimension is also predicted by psychological inflexibility and emotional dependence, obsessive preoccupation, self-conscious anxiety, and idealization (Marshall et al., 2025). The neglect dimension operates similarly, except it is not predicted by attachment orientation or idealization, and is associated with more social anxiety and lower self-esteem.

Whereas scholars have noted parallels between limerence and addiction and noted the potential path from limerence to stalking (e.g., Bradbury et al., 2025), there's reason to suggest that limerence can also serve as a coping mechanism in an unfulfilling relational context. Experiencing limerence can be a one-time experience or repeated, short-lived or long (Tennov, 1979), yet the context in which it occurs offers the suggestion that it is the mind's way of addressing an undermet need for belonging and intimacy. The field has much more to learn about limerence as an unusual manifestation of the human attachment system.

According to recent reports, bradbury, P., Short, E., & Bleakley, P. (2025). Limerence, hidden obsession, fixation, and rumination: A scoping review of human behaviour. Journal of Police and Criminal Psychology, 40(2), 417-426.

It has been revealed that marshall, L., Waldeck, D., Pancani, L., Churchill, S., & Tyndall, I. (2025). Development and validation of the Limerence Questionnaire (LQ-11). Psychological reports, 00332941251394980.

Sources indicate that verhulst, J. (1984). Limerence: Notes on the nature and function of passionate love. Psychoanalysis & Contemporary Thought, 7(1), 115–138.

Sources indicate that as many of Arc Raiders’ regular players predicted, the game’s first post-launch map won’t just be available for everyone, it will instead be closely tied to a community event. Breaking New Ground is the name of that event, and it’s one where everyone will need to contribute in order to rebuild some old tunnels and unlock the way to Stella Montis.

Industry observers note that the event kicks off today alongside the release of the game’s latest patch. The ask is relatively simple: players must commit Basic Materials to the project so that the tunnels can be rebuilt. This option will be available to anyone who’s played at least five rounds.

If you’ve spent any time in Arc Raiders, you’ll know that Basic Materials are things like Metal parts, Fabric, Chemicals, Rubber Parts, and Plastic Parts - most of which are easy to find in the game’s various maps.

Even beyond the ultimate goal of unlocking the new map, donations will also reward you with Merits, which is a new event currency, though there’s a cap on how many you can earn.

Once enough materials have been collected, the next phase of the event, Staking Our Claim, will begin, which will bring a new progression track to the game, and make Stella Montis available for players to visit.

Industry observers note that developer Embark describes the latest environment as unlike any that we have seen in the game so far. It’s a facility carved into the northern mountains, which means it’s going to have a near-pristine look; quite the contrast with the rest of the game’s environments.

Stella Montis also has its own Arc enemies, loot, schematics, and other gameplay items. You can look forward to coming across the Shredder, a close-quarter Arc unit exclusive to the upcoming map for now.

Then there’s The Matriarch, a somehow even larger version of the Queen. Thankfully, it will only be available under a specific map condition, so you’re in no danger of running into her randomly. The revision will also introduce a new legendary weapon, two new grenades, and three new mines.

Staking Our Claim will only run until December, which is when the next stage of the game’s roadmap will kick off. Then, the Cold Snap patch will introduce the Flickering Flames event, the first snowfall Map Condition, and the Expedition Project voluntary wipe.

In a recent development, ford has entered the battery business. The first LFP battery cells are now rolling off the assembly line at Ford’s BlueOval Battery Park plant in Michigan and are headed to power Fathom prototypes in Kentucky.

It has been revealed that how do you get more out of a battery without adding weight or more cells? According to Alan Clarke, Ford’s vice president of advanced development projects, who is also leading its Universal Electric Vehicle (UEV) platform, the answer lies in lithium iron phosphate (LFP) technology.

Unlike traditional lithium-ion, LFP batteries use no nickel or cobalt, which helps reduce costs. They also typically hold up better after years of use and charging.

According to recent reports, to make it a reality, Ford turned to CATL, the leading global EV battery manufacturer. Ford uses CATL’s licensed technology and manufacturing expertise at its BlueOval Battery Park Michigan plant.

Ford mentioned it will be the first in the US to deliver LFP batteries for mainstream automotive use, with the battery cells now rolling off the line in Michigan.

The first LFP battery cells are headed to Ford’s Louisville Assembly Plant and will be used to power Fathom prototypes, its first vehicle based on the UEV platform.

In a recent development, ford designed and engineered the Fathom from the ground up for efficiency. As such, it chose prismatic battery cells because they fit directly into the chassis, reducing structural costs.

With cells now being delivered from a plant that it owns and operates, Ford mentioned it will use the knowledge gained in Michigan to support more affordable EVs and Ford Energy, its new battery energy storage business in Kentucky.

At Ford’s new battery plant in Michigan, assembly lines can deliver 40 cells every minute, making it one of the fastest LFP prismatic battery assembly lines outside China.

Although the accelerated output drives down costs, Ford mentioned employees use AI-powered image recognition and inspection tools to spot defects in real time and maintain quality.

“Our goal is to make defective cells so rare that we track their frequency per billion cells rather than per million,” Ford remarked.

With production testing now underway, Ford prepares to have the battery pack plant in Michigan up and running in 2027, ahead of schedule.

Ford will open preorders for the Fathom in early 2027, starting at $28,350 for the standard-range model.

CEO Jim Farley mentioned on the organization’s third-quarter earnings call last month that the Fathom, Ford’s first vehicle based on the UEV platform, remains on track to launch in Q4 2027.

Farley stated the Fathom is a “breakthrough product” that’s highly capable and still affordable. The starting MSRP is under $30,000, and the low cost of ownership is perfect for today’s market, he added.

Ford and Slate both producing vehicles with US-produced LFP batteries is a great milestone. Hopefully we can keep pushing our domestic battery supply chain forward.

Ford noted the Fathom will offer more interior space than a Toyota RAV4, and it will cost less to own over five years than a three-year-old used Tesla Model Y.

Recent findings suggest that the pickup will be the first vehicle to integrate Apple Maps directly into the navigation system. All versions will be BlueCruise-capable for hands-free driving, with standard Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, plus bidirectional charging capabilities.

Although we have yet to see it, Ford said the Fathom features a “large touchscreen display” with easy-to-use navigation.

Ford has not revealed battery specs or range, but we do know the pickup will have an NACS port after several prototypes were spotted at a Tesla Supercharger over the summer.

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Peanut allergies have been on the rise in recent decades.
  • According to statistics provided by Food Allergy Research & Education (FARE), an estimated 6.2 million children and adults in the United States are allergic to peanuts.
  • However, newly introduced research published in the November 2026 matter of The Journal of Allergy and Clinical Immunology suggests that over a third of infants thought to have this diagnosis might not actually have a peanut allergy.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Peanut allergies have been on the rise in recent decades.

According to statistics provided by Food Allergy Research & Education (FARE), an estimated 6.2 million children and adults in the United States are allergic to peanuts.

However, newly introduced research published in the November 2026 matter of The Journal of Allergy and Clinical Immunology suggests that over a third of infants thought to have this diagnosis might not actually have a peanut allergy.

In fact, having a history of reacting to peanuts and positive allergy testing on their own may not be sufficient to diagnose a peanut allergy for many infants.

The study’s authors suggest that a threshold oral food challenge — in which the child is given increasing amounts of the suspected food allergen under medical supervision to look for an allergic reaction — should be routinely considered to help confirm peanut allergy.

This additional testing could safely prevent children who are not allergic to peanuts from undergoing unnecessary treatment with oral immunotherapy.

It could also spare families from burdensome food restrictions and allergy precautions.

The researchers’ goal was to evaluate the accuracy and safety of the Allergy Development to an Accelerated Path to Tolerance (ADAPT) peanut oral immunotherapy program, which was established in 2024 at 10 public children’s hospitals across Australia.

This program provides a standardized approach to evaluating and treating infants with suspected peanut allergies.

The study included infants who had experienced a mild to moderate reaction to peanut before 12 months of age and had evidence of peanut sensitization through allergy testing.

Researchers reviewed medical records to examine how accurately the program’s approach identified peanut allergies and whether it could safely guide treatment.

Industry observers note that A key part of the evaluation was a threshold oral food challenge. The challenge involved up to seven doses, ranging from 15 to 1,300 milligrams of peanut protein.

Medical teams monitored the infants for reactions and provided treatment when necessary.

Researchers reviewed records from April 2024 through October 2025. During that period, 1,275 infants were assessed through the program, and 778 underwent an oral food challenge.

The researchers also examined allergy test results and whether infants who reacted during the challenges could begin oral immunotherapy at an appropriate starting dose.

At the time of the oral food challenge, the infants had a median age of 13 months.

Of the 778 infants who underwent an oral food challenge, 507 (65.2%) had an allergic reaction.

However, 271 (34.8%) did not react to peanut during the supervised test, despite having a history of a previous reaction and positive allergy test results.

These findings suggest that relying on medical history and allergy tests alone may lead some infants to be labeled with a peanut allergy when they can actually tolerate the food.

Among the infants who reacted during the challenges, 61 experienced anaphylaxis, a severe allergic reaction that can affect breathing and blood pressure. This represented 12% of infants with a positive challenge and 7.8% of all infants who underwent testing. Medical teams safely managed these severe allergic reactions.

Researchers also found that infants who reacted to peanut generally had higher skin prick test results and Ara h 2-specific IgE levels than those who did not react.

However, these test results did not reliably indicate how much peanut would trigger a reaction or how severe that reaction would be.

Of the 394 infants who began peanut oral immunotherapy, 384 (97.5%) successfully started treatment at a dose below the amount that had triggered a reaction during their food challenge.

The researchers say these findings support considering supervised oral food challenges to confirm suspected peanut allergies before starting treatment or recommending long-term avoidance.

Erin Banta, MD, a board certified allergist and immunologist who treats both children and adults at Latitude Food Allergy Care in Great Neck, New York, noted these findings are significant because they provide evidence for early use of oral food challenges in infants with peanut reactions.

“In those with mild-moderate prior reactions to peanut, early oral food challenge may allow for either delabeling of food allergy (in 1/3 of the patients in this study) or diagnosis of food allergy,” she told Healthline.

Banta, who wasn’t involved in the study, added that early delabeling takes a significant burden off the patient and their family.

“On the other hand,” she explained, “early diagnosis allows for early initiation of treatment with oral immunotherapy at a time in the patient’s life associated with the greatest success rates.”.

Banta further noted that the study offers different pathways for oral immunotherapy based on the patient’s reaction threshold. This means that some patients may be able to complete treatment more promptly due to their individual threshold dose.

Lindsey Forstie, FNP, a family nurse practitioner with clinical training and experience in allergy and asthma care at Carefree Allergy in Phoenix, AZ, added that while further evaluation may be needed to confirm a peanut allergy diagnosis, it’s key for parents not to try introducing peanuts at home.

“Instead, they should speak with their pediatrician or allergist about appropriate testing and whether a supervised food challenge is safe and necessary,” she stated.

According to Forstie, who was also not part of the study, the goal is to avoid unnecessary food restrictions while also keeping children safe.

Sources indicate that “The key message is that not every positive allergy test means a child has a food allergy,” she told Healthline. “Accurate diagnosis helps protect children while allowing those who are not allergic to enjoy a more normal, less restrictive diet.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Decades before the advent of the soft-roader, Subaru was building everyday cars with a limited amount of extra off-road capability.
  • Recent findings suggest that naturally, Subaru has now combined the two by offering a Forester Hybrid in Wilderness trim.
  • Sources indicate that our expert editors test every vehicle we review.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Decades before the advent of the soft-roader, Subaru was building everyday cars with a limited amount of extra off-road capability. So it should be no surprise that its Wilderness line of slightly more capable crossovers has been a hit. So, too, has Subaru’s integration of hybrid systems, in an era when buyers of volume cars such as the Forester are happy to get their hands on anything that means greater efficiency.

Recent findings suggest that naturally, Subaru has now combined the two by offering a Forester Hybrid in Wilderness trim. The recipe seems like a sales hit waiting to happen, but is it worth the extra complexity?

Sources indicate that our expert editors test every vehicle we review. Read more about how we test and review cars here.

In a recent development, subaru finally brought a hybrid powertrain to the Forester for the 2025 model year. A latest Wilderness was introduced a few months later, but it lacked the gas-electric system available on the basic car. The Forester Wilderness Hybrid combines the two, allowing Subaru to offer a system peak of 194 horsepower from a 2.5-liter flat-four and a 1-kWh battery pack.

EPA-estimated fuel economy is down slightly from the basic Forester Hybrid, but the 33 mpg city and 29 mpg highway are still both solid numbers for a crossover with 9.3 inches of ground clearance and Yokohama Geolander all-terrain tires. For most buyers, that improvement alone should justify the price, which is $1000 more than the basic Forester Wilderness.

Powertrain: 2.5-liter Atkinson-cycle flat-four, lithium-ion hydride battery pack.

Power: 194 hp @ 5600 rpm (peak system output).

Transmission: continuously variable automatic, all-wheel drive.

EPA mpg: 33 city, 29 highway, 31 combined.

Recent findings suggest that befitting the Wilderness Hybrid’s soft-roader credentials, the media drive took place on the dirt, grass, and gravel roads of a private ranch. While this made for beautiful scenery, it did little to showcase what the car could do as a daily driver or challenge its off-road capabilities.

It has been revealed that those capabilities did impress on a more technical off-roading course that Subaru built for the event, although that comes with the caveat that the organization presumably built the course with the car’s limits in mind. Even though this is ultimately still a relatively conventional crossover with nothing like the articulation of a more extreme off-roader, the all-terrain tires were capable of handling substantial ruts and steep hill descents.

Industry observers note that approach, break-over, and departure angles of 23.5, 20.6, and 25.5 degrees, respectively, are identical to the nonhybrid Forester Wilderness. This hybrid crossover has the clearance to get over obstacles a car camper or kayaker might find on the trail to their favorite outdoor-recreation spot. The biggest frustration here was the low resolution of the X-Drive off-road menus built into the infotainment screens, a feature that felt behind the respectable capabilities of the crossover itself.

According to recent reports, while the off-road performance is what sets the Wilderness apart from its more pedestrian Forester Hybrid brethren, limited on-road testing suggests that the car feels similar in everyday situations. Given the all-terrain tires, that’s a solid achievement, even if the end result is still relative mediocrity. This Forester is no performance car, and anyone who might have been expecting a canyon carver will instead have to make do with relaxed acceleration and a frustrating continuously variable automatic transmission.

According to recent reports, the Forester is a tentpole for Subaru because it combines the basic compact-crossover shape today’s buyers want with some degree of utility in all forms. The Wilderness goes one step further in providing even more capability, but its day-to-day strength will be how little it sacrifices to do that.

The Forester Wilderness Hybrid drops 5 mpg of efficiency in the city in comparison to the standard Forester Hybrid, for 33 mpg. The basic Forester Wilderness, by contrast, gets just 24 mpg in the city. The hybrid remains relatively comfortable and quiet on the road too, which is great news for buyers who do not want to hear harsh noises from all-terrain tires and the unique drone of a Subaru boxer engine all day.

Recent findings suggest that still, the Wilderness line is differentiated by its capabilities. Buyers looking for a soft-roader do expect to use the car on a trail every so often, which makes the Wilderness Hybrid’s lack of a spare tire a major matter. Since components of the hybrid system are packed where a spare would go on a normal Wilderness, buyers of this car will either have to find another way to carry a fifth tire or contend with the reality that a flat could derail their outdoor adventures in a worse way than the same problem would in the nonhybrid model.

In a recent development, that missing spare tire is one of two major drawbacks for the Wilderness Hybrid. The other is the towing capacity, down from 3500 pounds to just 1500. Both of these are serious limitations for buyers who have certain use cases in mind for their soft-roader, but neither is necessarily a problem for the average buyer. The price difference is not negligible, but fuel savings should cover the difference in cost within a few years. For most buyers, that makes the Hybrid the obvious choice.

Buyers looking at other hybrid soft-roaders could also consider the new Toyota RAV4 Woodland and the Honda CR-V Trailsport. The Subaru is the only one of the three hybrids with conventional full-time all-wheel drive, although that specific differentiator is not necessarily a game changer for buyers who will be spending most of their time on the street. For those who do need to venture a little further a little more often, though, the Forester Hybrid Wilderness seems like the strongest choice.

Industry observers note that subaru’s Wilderness models are sold with synthetic StarTex interiors meant to be easily cleaned, and this particular vehicle even includes a synthetic steering-wheel cover in lieu of the usual leather. This is a small detail for most, but it does mean that the cabin is entirely vegan. For some very specific buyers, however, that one detail could make all the difference.

The Men’s Health GLP-1 Holiday Survival Guide

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Our product picks are editor-tested, expert-approved.
  • THE HOLIDAYS AND GLP-1 can feel like a cruel joke.
  • A POPULAR STRATEGY is to skip a dose for the holiday week.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Our product picks are editor-tested, expert-approved. We may earn a commission through links on our site. Why Trust Us?

THE HOLIDAYS AND GLP-1 can feel like a cruel joke. Mashed potatoes and gravy? Come on. Pumpkin pie? Dude. Your grandma’s urge to Eat! Eat! What’s wrong with you? It can be a lot.Luckily, we’re far enough along in this whole GLP-1 experience that researchers and experts now know how people who take the weight-loss medications can not only survive the holidays—but actually enjoy them, gravy and all. We talked to some of these smart people to come up with your GLP-1 game plan—both at the table, and for around the table when those relatives you only see once a year get sassy.

A POPULAR STRATEGY is to skip a dose for the holiday week. But doctors tend to recommend against this strategy.

Vijay Kasi, MD, PhD, cardiologist at Orlando Health says that you might even experience short-term changes in blood pressure and blood sugar spikes, which is really only a concern if you are diabetic. Now would missing one GLP-1 dose severely impact the heart? Not really.

Dr. Kasi says increased risk for cardiac events is more likely to happen when people quit the medication for good and slide back to unhealthy eating habits. A 2026 study found that any heart benefit from taking a GLP-1 disappears after two years. Those same people were linked to a 22 percent increased risk of stroke, heart attacks, and early death.

But again, we’re talking about a week—not two years. So what’s wrong with resuming a day or two after the holiday? If you are still adamant about skipping a dose, resuming it immediately after is recommended. “If they ate a really large meal and then immediately took the medication, they may feel very uncomfortable,” notes Mir Ali, MD, medical director of MemorialCare Surgical Weight Loss Center at Orange Coast Medical Center. “But if they wait 24 hours and the meal has moved through their system, then it probably won't be as problematic.”.

The real concern doctors have is if people continue to delay their GLP-1 schedule for multiple weeks. Dr. Ali claims people stop feeling the effects a week after they stop the medication because that’s how long it stays in your system. Appetite returns and so does food noise—the persistent and intrusive thoughts related to cravings or obsessing over how much food you ate. Ashley Koff, RD, author of Your Best Shot, says other issues that may promote overeating are that you no longer have a delay in gastric emptying and an alteration or sheer lack of fullness signaling. “When you stop this medication abruptly you go from [constant] sustained hormone back to your own which works at best for 2 to 5 minutes when triggered by food,” she says.

Recent findings suggest that while one day of eating more than usual won’t make a significant change to your health, Dr. Kasi indicates that some people do struggle to get back on track after the holidays end. “For a few people, it may be easy, but a vast majority trying to break away from their established regimen might have problems.”.

Industry observers note that DOCTORS ARE GENERALLY against taking a smaller dose than usual because it is not included in FDA guidelines for how to safely and effectively use a GLP-1. “If a lower dose wasn't effective for you beforehand, it's not going to be effective for you right before a holiday either,” notes Dr. Ali. “It’s similar to skipping a dose.”.

Sources indicate that there is one exception. Dr. Ali claims people who have attained a healthy weight or reached their goal weight may be able to lower their dose or take it less frequently as a maintenance strategy.

According to recent reports, “For some people who have been on it for a long time, they titrate down to the most effective dose,” indicates Heidi Skolnik, MS, CDN, nutritionist and author of Your GLP-1 Game Strategy. “You're trying to find what's the lowest amount that still is effective for you.”.

Industry observers note that lowering your GLP-1 dose is a conversation you’ll want to have with your doctor ahead of the holiday season. Experts say to avoid self-prescribing.

Sources indicate that IF YOU’RE ON a GLP-1, your plate will likely look different from your relatives who are scooping up substantial portions of carb-heavy sides. With a lower tolerance for small portions and a change in appetite, your choices will involve a delicate balance of trying to meet your nutritional needs while also not making your stomach hurt from overindulging. You can, of course, still enjoy as many courses as you like.

If you are going to someone’s house, Skolnik advises calling ahead and asking what’s on the menu so you can plan in advance. For appetizers, you’ll want to avoid any high-fat items. “It's okay if you don't hit your protein and fiber goals. But what you don't want to do is eat a lot of high fat,” she indicates. “This is because your gastric system is slowing down. With high-fat foods, you may not digest all of that.”.

Not sure what’s high-fat or not? Play it safe and bring your own appetizer. Not only are you being a hospitable guest, but you’ll have something you can eat. Skolnik recommends:.

Don’t think that you’re banned from eating any certain foods, but with small portions, you have to know if it’s worth indulging. Koff claims to use the "Delicious to Me" rule. Stop after the first bite to assess how much you enjoy the food. “I give them what that means on a scale they devise from 1 to 10, where a 7 or greater means it’s delicious and a go.”.

Recent findings suggest that so include those carb-heavy sides like mac and cheese and creamy mashed potatoes—just keep it to around a quarter of your plate. The majority of your plate should include a mix of vegetables and protein, which Skolnik says is usually manageable with turkey.

In a recent development, common side effects of GLP-1 use include nausea from drinking and a reduced craving for alcohol. If you can tolerate one or two, both dietitians say to go for it. A drinking variation of the “Delicious to Me” strategy is the “9 Sips” rule. “You still need to factor in what sugar, caffeine, and alcohol will do but a smaller amount is the win while still enjoying,” states Koff. You’ll also want to drink water at regular intervals while you’re drinking.

Recent findings suggest that if you want to avoid being pressured into drinking, Skolnik states to also have a drink on hand with a lime slice to give the appearance of an alcoholic drink. “Nobody has to know what's in your glass.”.

No need to ruin a favorite dessert by trying to choose only high-protein items. If you want to save your appetite for an extra slice of pie, Koff indicates to go for it. Just make sure to meet your nutritional needs in different ways as with a protein drink before dinner or supplements.

IT’S NOT JUST the food you need to navigate; the interactions matter too. Depending on your family situation, you may need to set some firm boundaries on or redirect comments related to your weight or appetite. That doesn’t mean the holidays are the time to announce to everyone you’re on a GLP-1 (unless you want to). Some phrases you can use include:.

Skolnik claims having an ally is extremely crucial if you’re expecting other people to comment on your eating habits or your looks. They can help to redirect any uncomfortable conversation, provide support for your choices so you don’t feel isolated, or just provide emotional support. “Have someone else in the room with a code word or a look that signals them to intervene and change the conversation or divert attention away,” she says.

According to recent reports, even if you don’t have an ally physically next to you, have someone available on the phone that you can text or call. Skolnik states to escape to the bathroom if you need and use it as a place to recenter.

To avoid offending people who probably spent hours cooking, it can also be helpful to practice polite ways to turn down second helpings or pass on specific dishes.

According to recent reports, “When the giving of food is looked at as love, the receiving of it is love,” indicates Skolnik. “But you can still receive the love without the food.”.

Industry observers note that jocelyn Solis-Moreira, MS is the associate health & fitness for Men's Health and has previously written for CNN, Scientific American, Popular Science, and National Geographic before joining the brand. When she's not working, she's doing circus arts or working towards the perfect pull-up.
