5 Evidence-Based Treatments for Borderline Personality Disorder

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1054 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Posted November 20, 2026 | Reviewed by Monica Vilhauer Ph.D.
  • Recent findings suggest that for a long time, borderline personality disorder (BPD) was considered one of the most difficult mental health conditions to treat.
  • It has been revealed that fortunately, decades of research have demonstrated otherwise.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 20, 2026 | Reviewed by Monica Vilhauer Ph.D.

Recent findings suggest that for a long time, borderline personality disorder (BPD) was considered one of the most difficult mental health conditions to treat. Some therapists even believed that people with BPD couldn't get better.

It has been revealed that fortunately, decades of research have demonstrated otherwise. Today, several treatments can help people with BPD manage intense emotions, build healthier relationships, and reduce impulsive behaviors.

Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT) is probably the best known, but it's not the only option. Here are five approaches worth considering if you're looking for care for yourself or a loved one.

Developed by psychologist Marsha Linehan, DBT was the first treatment for BPD to demonstrate effectiveness in a randomized clinical trial.

According to recent reports, the results were incredibly promising. Among chronically suicidal women with BPD, those receiving DBT engaged in less self-harm, had fewer psychiatric hospitalizations, and were more likely to stay in treatment than those receiving usual care.

Since then, DBT has been evaluated in dozens of randomized clinical trials. Its strongest evidence is for reducing suicidal and self-injurious behaviors, although promising findings extend to substance use, eating disorders, and depression.

DBT is based on the idea that people with BPD experience emotions intensely and may rely on coping strategies that provide temporary relief but create problems in the long run.

According to the treatment manual, comprehensive (full model) DBT programs include several components: weekly individual therapy, weekly skills group, and between-session phone coaching. In individual therapy, it is common to review difficulties that came up during the week and explore alternative responses. In skills group, patients receive didactic (class-like) instruction in four skill areas: mindfulness, emotion regulation, distress tolerance, and interpersonal effectiveness. Between-session phone coaching helps people apply these skills when they need them most.

It has been revealed that initially, Marsha Linehan recommended that people with BPD make a year-long commitment to their DBT program. However, many DBT programs now offer care for shorter durations (e.g., 6 months).

Developed by psychologist Peter Fonagy and psychiatrist Anthony Bateman, MBT has demonstrated improvements in BPD symptoms, self-harm, and interpersonal functioning in randomized clinical trials.

Sources indicate that MBT focuses on improving mentalizing, our ability to understand our own thoughts and feelings and those of others. Rather than explicitly teaching coping skills, as in DBT, therapists help patients strengthen this ability through interactions during therapy.

Industry observers note that for example, imagine leaving a session convinced your therapist was annoyed with you. Rather than simply reassuring you, an MBT therapist might explore what happened and what each of you might have been thinking or feeling.

Recent findings suggest that the therapeutic relationship becomes a place to practice navigating emotionally charged interactions. Treatment typically includes weekly individual and group sessions over 12–18 months.

Developed by psychiatrist Otto Kernberg and colleagues, TFP has demonstrated improvements in BPD symptoms and interpersonal functioning in randomized clinical trials.

According to recent reports, like MBT, TFP focuses on relationships rather than teaching specific coping skills. However, TFP emphasizes difficulties integrating positive and negative perceptions of ourselves and others.

Industry observers note that for example, someone with BPD might see their partner as loving and trustworthy one moment, but cruel and uncaring after a disagreement. TFP helps patients recognize that positive and negative qualities can exist in the same person.

Treatment typically involves twice-weekly individual sessions lasting a year or longer.

Developed by psychiatrist John Gunderson, GPM takes a different approach; the goal is to make effective BPD treatment accessible through generalist mental health clinicians.

Rather than requiring extensive training in specialized psychotherapy, GPM provides a practical framework for understanding BPD, managing crises, and improving everyday functioning.

Industry observers note that particular attention is given to relationships, work, school, and other meaningful activities. Treatment typically involves weekly appointments, with flexibility based on patients' needs.

Importantly, a randomized clinical trial comparing general psychiatric management with DBT found substantial improvements in both groups, including reductions in suicidal and self-injurious behaviors.

This work challenged the assumption that effective BPD treatment necessarily requires a highly specialized, intensive program.

BPD Compass is a newer cognitive-behavioral treatment my colleagues and I developed to make evidence-based BPD care more efficient and accessible.

Recent findings suggest that we were intrigued that existing treatments all produce meaningful improvements, with no single approach consistently outperforming the others. This suggests that each addresses something key, whether that's emotion regulation (DBT), relationships (MBT, TFP), or building a meaningful life (GPM).

Yet many patients continue experiencing symptoms after treatment. We wondered whether nonresponse might reflect a mismatch between patients' difficulties and the treatment they receive.

In a recent development, we designed BPD Compass to address three broad vulnerabilities associated with BPD: emotion dysregulation, relationship difficulties, and impulsivity. In our clinical trials, treatment begins with an assessment to identify which patterns are driving a particular patient's symptoms, followed by an individualized blueprint emphasizing the most relevant modules.

Sources indicate that BPD Compass takes 18 sessions, considerably shorter than many established BPD treatments. Like GPM, it was designed for generalist clinicians without requiring extensive specialized training.

According to recent reports, in an initial randomized clinical trial, participants receiving BPD Compass demonstrated large improvements in BPD symptoms. Subsequent research also documented improvements in emotional, relational, and impulsive functioning, as well as symptoms of co-occurring conditions.

BPD is an incredibly heterogeneous condition. Some people experience frequent suicidal crises and need intensive, long-term support. Others may make meaningful progress with a shorter intervention.

As a BPD treatment developer, my goal isn't to replace existing treatments. It's to expand the options available. Not everyone with BPD needs year-long therapy, and we should have effective, personalized alternatives for those who don't.

Ultimately, the best treatment is one that addresses your difficulties, provides the support you need, and is accessible enough for you to receive it.

According to recent reports, if you or someone you love is contemplating suicide, seek help immediately. For help 24/7, dial 988 for the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline, or reach out to the Crisis Text Line by texting TALK to 741741. To find a therapist near you, visit the Psychology Today Therapy Directory.

Zenless Zone Zero’s latest Special Program was a significant one, bringing us all the news about Version 2.4, the next major update. It’s called On the Precipice of the Abyss, and it will be available to download on November 26.

On the Precipice of the Abyss has tendrils in many areas of the game, touching several parts of its fiction as well as gameplay, so it’s one to watch out for.

Version 2.4’s biggest claim to fame is the introduction of the Krampus Compliance Authority, a new faction that’s affiliated with TOPS. This looks to be the oversight committee, dispatched after the squad’s adventure beneath Timesworn Hill.

Sources indicate that the events of this narrative arch follow on from the Timesworn Hill crisis, which is partly why we’re going to a new area as part of this update. The old mining site can now be explored for the first time in a decade, now that the Miasma has begun to recede.

Our newcomers this time around are Dialyn and Banyue. Dialyn is an S-Rank Physical Stun Agent who’s a former customer service specialist. This isn’t just a backstory, however, as it plays into her gameplay.

Dialyn relies on two resources: Customer Complaint and Positive Review, but her core role is to stun enemies and allow teammates to unleash their Ults, with a nice boost to boot.

Banyue is another S-Rank, though he’s a Fire Rupture Agent. He uses his martial arts expertise to create combinations of might and grandeur. In combat, he pulls from Adrenaline and Wrathful Fires, alternating between the two to fuel his actions. There’s a bit of rhythm to his gameplay that might take you a little while to master.

Even more characters will join as part of this revision, in the form of not one but two new Bangboo units. Birkblick is Krampus' own proprietary lil bunny fella, who brings a sensor array that can transform into a cannon in combat, essentially tracking and immediately nuking targets. Then there’s Bild N. Boolok, a Support Agent-affiliated Physical damage dealing Bangboo bringing a giant block hammer to the fight to, well, smash enemies with.

It’s a bit of a winter party in Version 2.4, it seems, as the revision will bring back Hugo (Attack - Ice), and Ellen (Attack - Ice), too.

You can also look forward to the return of the Bangboo auto chess event, which now includes PvE stages with unique rewards. In fact, playing this event is how you could get Bild N. Boolok for free. Lightstream Notes is another event that will be available for the duration of this revision, and it will let you tag along with Ye Shunguang to New Eridu.

High Fat Diet Linked to Higher Colon Cancer Risk, Early Research Reveals

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1271 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Healthline

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a fresh study, researchers report that a high fat diet may potentially increase the risk of colon cancer.
  • The researchers from Arizona State University stated a diet high in certain fats can cause lasting changes in intestinal stem cells that lead to the development of tumors and the possibility of colon cancer.
  • The study was conducted in mice, but the researchers noted changes in the DNA of intestinal stem cells that may explain their growth and survival.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a fresh study, researchers report that a high fat diet may potentially increase the risk of colon cancer.

The researchers from Arizona State University stated a diet high in certain fats can cause lasting changes in intestinal stem cells that lead to the development of tumors and the possibility of colon cancer.

The study was conducted in mice, but the researchers noted changes in the DNA of intestinal stem cells that may explain their growth and survival.

The researchers published their findings on November 12 in the journal Stem Cell Reports.

Sources indicate that the researchers remarked the study is crucial because 1 in 25 people develop colon cancer in their lifetime. In the United States, that translates into about 108,000 latest cases of colon cancer every year. About 55,000 males and 55,000 females are expected to die from the disease in 2026.

Experts not involved in the study say the research provides valuable information, but they have reservations about the results, as the findings do not yet apply to humans.

“The findings provide a potential mechanism linking diet to intestinal cancer development, but we need to be cautious about translating these results to humans,” said Dalia Perelman, MS, CDE, a research dietitian at Stanford University in California.

“We already have evidence from human studies that obesity and certain dietary patterns, particularly those high in processed meats and low in fiber-rich foods, are associated with increased colorectal cancer risk,” Perelman told Healthline. “This study adds a potentially important mechanism to investigate, but it does not establish that dietary fat itself increases colorectal cancer risk in humans.”.

Ketan Thanki, MD, a colorectal surgeon specializing in benign and malignant diseases of the colon, rectum, and anus at the MemorialCare Todd Cancer Institute at Long Beach Medical Center in California, shared similar views.

“This study provides a better understanding at the cellular level of how a high fat diet may contribute to colorectal cancer development,” Thanki told Healthline.

Recent findings suggest that “Animal studies are an key starting point for understanding biological processes, but we must be cautious about directly applying their findings to humans,” he added. “Mice and humans share many cellular and biological mechanisms, which makes these studies valuable in identifying potential pathways involved in disease development. However, human diets, genetics, metabolism, and environmental exposures are more complex.”.

To reach their findings, the Arizona State researchers fed mice what the scientists described as a Western-style high fat diet for 6 months.

They then compared those results with those from mice given a low fat diet.

In a recent development, the researchers said the mice on the high fat diet gained more weight than the mice on the low-fat diet. They also developed more intestinal stem cells, and those cells grew at a more rapid rate.

They added that mice genetically predisposed to intestinal cancer who were fed a high-fat diet developed more and larger tumors.

The researchers noted changes in the DNA of intestinal stem cells that may help explain their increased growth and survival.

They also pointed out that stem cell behavior returned to normal after high fat diet mice were switched to a low fat diet, although some DNA changes persisted. After four weeks, approximately 18% of these changes remained.

When mice were returned to a high fat diet, the researchers said their intestinal stem cells responded more swiftly and strongly than those of mice exposed to the diet for the first time.

They concluded that the study suggests that maintaining a healthy, low fat diet may help regulate intestinal stem cell growth and reduce colon cancer risk.

Kristin Kirkpatrick, RD, president of KAK Consulting and a dietitian at the Cleveland Clinic Department of Wellness & Preventive Medicine in Ohio, wasn’t involved in the study but highlighted a particular aspect of the findings.

“What I found particularly interesting was that even after the mice returned to a low fat diet, some of the molecular changes persisted,” she told Healthline. “This raises questions about how our dietary patterns over time may influence long-term health.”.

Experts said these new findings are interesting but noted numerous caveats.

“One notable takeaway is that dietary habits over time matter,” mentioned Thanki. “Even if someone has consumed a high fat diet for years, making changes now may still provide meaningful health benefits.”.

“I also think these findings are particularly crucial for children and adolescents, as establishing healthier dietary habits early in life may provide long-term benefits,” he added.

Recent findings suggest that however, Thanki noted that not all fats are the same. “The health risks depend partly on the type of fat consumed, how much is consumed, and what foods make up the overall diet,” he said.

In a recent development, “Diets consistently high in saturated fats, particularly those containing large amounts of processed meats, fried foods, and highly processed products, can contribute to obesity, elevated cholesterol, cardiovascular disease, and metabolic dysfunction. These factors can also contribute to chronic inflammation and may increase the risk of certain cancers, including colorectal cancer,” Thanki continued.

Perelman stated the diet used in the study was extremely high in fat, providing 60% of calories from fat, primarily from lard.

“We know that the health effects of dietary fats differ depending on their sources and fatty acid composition, and we cannot assume that a diet rich in unsaturated fats from foods such as olive oil, nuts, and seeds would produce the same effects,” she noted.

Perelman added that the researchers primarily studied stem cells from the small intestine rather than the colon.

“Although these tissues share some biological characteristics, they have vital differences, and we cannot assume that the same changes would occur in the colon,” she explained.

Finally, Perelman noted that “the mice consuming the high fat diet also gained weight, making it difficult to separate the effects of dietary fat itself from those associated with increased body fat and other metabolic changes.”.

Sources indicate that not all high fat foods are unhealthy. Some high fat foods that offer healthy benefits include:.

“The goal shouldn’t necessarily be to eliminate fat because our bodies need healthy fats for normal functioning,” noted Thanki. “Instead, people should focus on reducing saturated and trans fats while incorporating healthier unsaturated fats in appropriate amounts.”.

Thanki had several dietary suggestions. Among them:.

According to recent reports, “Consistency matters more than perfection. Even modest dietary changes, maintained over time, can have meaningful health benefits,” Thanki stated.

Sources indicate that perelman agreed. “The overall quality of the diet matters. Diets that are very high in fat may displace other foods and nutrients that have vital health benefits,” she stated.

“For colorectal cancer specifically, higher intakes of dietary fiber and whole grains have consistently been associated with lower risk,” Perelman noted.

“Therefore, rather than focusing exclusively on reducing fat, it is important to consider the overall dietary pattern and whether it provides adequate amounts of fiber-rich plant foods and other beneficial nutrients.”.

Kirkpatrick agreed that the type of fat is what is important. “A Mediterranean-style diet that includes olive oil, nuts, seeds, and fatty fish can be relatively high in fat but is consistently associated with positive health outcomes,” she remarked.

“On the other hand, a diet high in saturated fat, processed meats, and ultra-processed foods may increase the risk of certain chronic diseases, particularly when it’s also low in fiber and other protective nutrients.”.

Kirkpatrick also noted that many lifestyle habits contribute to a person’s overall health.

“Our health is influenced by so many factors beyond diet, including how we manage stress, our sleep habits, physical activity, genetics, and overall lifestyle,” she said.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • For starters, Ford’s standard 5.0-liter V-8 is mated here to a 3.0-liter Whipple supercharger for a total output of 840 horsepower and 615 lb-ft of torque.
  • “The Vintage Fastback is a car we’ve always wanted to build.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Taking a vintage muscle car and swapping in modern components to make it run better or add power is a story as old as, well, the LS2 V-8. Vintage Modern’s fresh Fastback Mustang turns that formula upside down—by swapping old-school body parts onto a modern S650-generation Mustang GT. But the Vintage Modern Fastback, officially revealed on Wednesday at Retromobile New York, is more than just a body kit.

For starters, Ford’s standard 5.0-liter V-8 is mated here to a 3.0-liter Whipple supercharger for a total output of 840 horsepower and 615 lb-ft of torque. Prospective buyers can choose between a six-speed manual transmission with rev matching or a 10-speed automatic with steering-wheel-mounted paddle shifters. Other high-end Mustang features like active-valve performance exhaust with four sound modes, MagneRide adaptive suspension, six selectable drive modes, and Brembo performance brakes are also standard fare.

“The Vintage Fastback is a car we’ve always wanted to build. We’ve blended classic-inspired design with modern safety, technology, and performance,” stated Chau Nguyen, founder and CEO of Vintage Modern. “This is what Vintage Modern was created to do.”.

Even though the bones of the Fastback are from a current-generation Mustang, the heavily modified vehicle still underwent crash testing to meet applicable Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards. This retro-inspired Mustang features eight airbags, crumple zones, side-impact beams, electronic stability control, traction control, and anti-lock brakes. That’s more than most restomod Mustang owners can say.

Recent findings suggest that most of the custom body panels, including the functional hood scoop, are carbon fiber; the only obviously metal pieces are the billet-aluminum grille, door handles, mirrors, and twin auxiliary driving lights. Similarly, the interior of the retro Fastback build features Alcantara and billet-aluminum trim over three different seat upholsteries: pleated, diamond-quilted, or woven. Each buyer can choose from more than 40 standard paint colors, as well as paint-to-sample finishes and stripe options, along with their own interior configurations; Vintage Modern is also offering an optional JL Audio premium sound system and leather-trimmed floor mats.

In a recent development, vintage Modern’s carbon-fiber body panels are hand-made in Detroit before being assembled and finished at its Atlanta facility; all told, each unit requires around 900 hours of hands-on labor. The builder has substantial prepares, too; it states it has plans to move into a new factory three times the size of its existing facility, hire more than 100 additional team members, and triple production capacity within two years.

No pricing details about the Vintage Modern Fastback were available at the time of publication, but we’ll enhancement this story when we learn more.

A Latest York transplant hailing from the Pacific Northwest, Emmet White has a passion for anything that goes: cars, bicycles, planes, and motorcycles. After learning to ride at 17, Emmet worked in the motorcycle industry before joining Autoweek in 2022 and Road & Track in 2024. The woes of alternate side parking have kept his fleet moderate, with a 2014 Volkswagen Jetta GLI and a BMW 318i E30 street parked in his Queens community.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Sources indicate that after a particularly strong 2025—movies like One Battle After Another and Sinners proved to be true standouts—how does 2026 pick up?

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AS A HUGE fan and follower of both movies and sports, the former has one major advantage: There's always something to look forward to. As a fan of the Fresh York Jets, I don't always have that luxury. As a fan of watching films, though, not only is there always something worth my time on the big screen or streaming, but there's always several flicks down the line that will sound great or intriguing for one reason or another. Will they all turn out great? Of course not. But with sports and movies alike, excitement tends to be all about hope.

Sources indicate that after a particularly strong 2025—movies like One Battle After Another and Sinners proved to be true standouts—how does 2026 pick up? With strength and energy, that's how. The year has been filled with all sorts of great movies, from horror (like 28 Years Later: The Bone Temple and Obsession) to epics (like The Odyssey), to some pretty great comedies (like Nirvanna the Band the Show the Movie and The Invite). It’s been a good year.

Industry observers note that but we always like to look at not only what’s been good to date, but also what we can still be excited for—and that includes everything. We’re talking stuff on the calendar already, stuff we suspect could come out this year, and even stuff making noise in places like the Sundance Film Festival. Throughout the year, this list evolves from our most anticpated movies into our favorite movies, and always looks quite different in December than it did in January.

Industry observers note that for now, we've got a lot we’ve loved, but still a lot to look forward to as well. Below, we've listed nearly 100 movies on our radar that we think you'll be really interested in seeing.

If you're interested in a killer chimpanzee B-movie slasher, then Primate is for you. The movie delivers what it promises. Ben the chimpanzee does some very terrible things on screen but it makes for quite an enjoyable experience.

28 Years Later: The Bone Temple.

28 Years Later: The Bone Temple is a direct sequel to last year's 28 Years Later. And while the great Danny Boyle doesn't return to direct, the movie is helmed by the more-than-capable Nia DaCosta and once again counts Alex Garland as its screenwriter. The real assets, though, are the movie's leads: Ralph Fiennes and Jack O'Connell are sensational, magnetic every minute they're on screen amidst all sorts of post-apocalyptic chaos. Bring on part three.

Here's a quick pitch for The Rip: Matt Damon and Ben Affleck. The longtime friends team up once again for The Rip, a cop thriller in the vein of movies you've probably seen several times before... but done particularly well. This twisty crime story involves a police team finding a ton of money in a stash house (the titular rip), and figuring out who may or may not be corrupt. In addition to our beloved duo, the cast is shockingly stacked: Steven Yeun, Kyle Chandler, Scott Adkins, and One Battle After AnotherAcademy Award nominee Teyana Taylor are all on board.

SAM RAIMI FANS, ASSEMBLE! For the first time since 2009, the master of gross effects and frenetic cameras is back with an original horror story in Send Help. Rachel McAdams plays a Survivor superfan who gets stuck on an island with her dickhead boss (Dylan O'Brien), and then the antics begin. Think Cast Away meets Misery meets Drag Me to Hell. It's great stuff.

According to recent reports, jason Momoa and Dave Bautista are a pair of cool dudes who, with The Wrecking Crew, set out and did exactly what they intended to do: Make a badass buddy action comedy. The movie finds the pair playing estranged brothers who reunite in Hawaii to investigate their father's mysterious death; From there, we get lots of jokes, and a lot of (very violent!!!) action. It's a good time! Honestly, if they want to make a couple sequels to this, I'd be her for it.

In a recent development, part This Is Spinal Tap, part Josie and the Pussycats, and part Curb Your Enthusiasm, The Moment is Charli XCX's movie for anyone who enjoys her music, persona, or both. A really fun movie about music, stardom, and celebrity in 2026.

Sources indicate that pillion was technically released initially in 2025 (and was also included on our list of favorite movies of that year), but we didn't want to miss an opportunity to recommend it to people once again. This unique film follows a man (Harry Melling) who engages in an unexpected BDSM relationship with a biker he meets at random (Alexander Skarsgård). The movie is quite the tonal balancing act, at times funny, intense, raunchy, and heartbreaking, but it all comes together by the end. A delightful movie, and a great showcase for both leads.

Sources indicate that the classic novel comes to life on the big screen once again, this time from Promising Young Woman and Saltburn director Emerald Fennell, and with Margot Robbie and Jacob Elordi in the lead roles. Fennell, an Academy Award winner for her work on Promising Young Woman, has both big fans and big detractors at this point—but her take her, while book purists haven't been thrilled, is a big, visually stunning epic romance. Robbie and Elordi are both up to the task as well, bringing a charged energy to roles that really need it. Alison Oliver, who recently shined on HBO's Task, is another major highlight in a supporting role. An original soundtrack from Charli XCX helps to set the anachronistic mood and feels like a real cherry on top.

Recent findings suggest that this action-thriller, based on a book by Don Winslow, looks like a very solid entry in the genre that we're going to call "Somewhat Resembles a Michael Mann Film." And reviews have confirmed as much—the movie has often been compared to Heat, and while its tough to compare to Mann's 1995 masterpiece, we'll take just about anything in that vein. Look: If someone tells you there's gonna be a crime thriller in the vein of Heat with Chris Hemsworth, Mark Ruffalo, Halle Berry, and Barry Keoghan leading the cast, how could you not be on board?

Recent findings suggest that one of our coolest directors, Gore Verbinski, makes his grand return with Good Luck, Have Fun, Don't Die—his first movie since 2016's A Cure For Wellness. If you don't know Verbinski by name, you should know several of his movies: the original Pirates of the Caribbean trilogy, The Ring, and Rango are among the standouts. Good Luck follows Sam Rockwell as a man who claims to be from the future and fighting off a rogue artificial intelligence. While the movie takes some pretty tough and labored tangents into on-the-nose satire, Rockwell's performance and the practical effects keep the movie afloat as a fun sci-fi romp.

Nirvanna the Band the Show the Movie.

Despite the title, you don't need to know anything else about Nirvanna the Band the Show the Movie before going to see it. Sure, this story of two inept dudes in a band who just want to play music at a bar—and go through all sorts of ordeals, including time-travel, to do it—has existed before in both web series and television series form. But you can just go in and laugh and the absolute madness of the movie. Trust us—you'll have a good time with this one if you're into "madness that makes you laugh." This is a long-term passion project of Matt Johnson, who became well known recently for directing the underrated BlackBerry. His brash talent is again on display here.

Industry observers note that we're always in on Glen Powell, and How to Make a Killing marks his first foray into A24's world as a leading man. This black comedy neo-noir comes from Emily the Criminal director John Patton Ford and follows Powell as a man who decides to take out a few members of his family in order to increase his chance at making a whole bunch of money via inheritance. The supporting cast joining Powell isn't too shabby: Margaret Qualley, Jessica Henwick, Ed Harris, and Topher Grace are all along for the fun.

According to recent reports, the Napa Boys is a very specific cut for comedy fans. Remember when all those nondescript American Pie direct-to-video sequels were coming out? "American Pie Presents:.."? The Napa Boys imagines itself as one of those: self-impressed raunchy comedy with little tact—crossed, naturally with the wine bro nature of 2004's Sideways. As a result, we get a movie that presents as a sequel to a franchise that both has long been running out of juice, and, in our world, never was. If you get the truly absurd brand of parody being presented here, you're going to get a real kick out of it.

Sources indicate that hoppers feels like a throwback to the golden age of Pixar. Not only is it an original story (at a time when the legendary animation studio has often been leaning into sequels, prequels, and more), but it's a sweet and funny one at that. Following an animal-lover who uses Avatar-style technology to transfer her consciousness into a robotic beaver body that can discover what animals are thinking and saying, Hoppers actually turns into something of a conspiracy mystery story. With a voice cast that includes Jon Hamm, Dave Franco, and Meryl Streep among others, it's a fun one for the whole family.

Look. This is one of those movies that you really don't have to overthink. It's Alan Ritchson—Reacher himself—taking on a giant alien robot monster thing. This is as much of a throwback to '80s-style action filmmaking as we're ever going to get, and it delivers as promised. The fact that the rest of the cast includes staples like Jai Courtney, Esai Morales, and Dennis Quaid is just a bonus.

Undertone has been positioning itself as A24's next huge horror hit—and we'll see how it lands. The filmfollows a supernatural podcaster who gets sent some particularly spooky recordings; Its soundscape has brought tons of hype, with many calling it the scariest experience of the year. A simple premise like that sometimes makes for a very solid horror movie.

Industry observers note that based on the novel by Andy Weir(who also wrote The Martian), Project Hail Mary is a story of space exploration and a regular guy (played by Ryan Gosling) who gets involved. Phil Lord and Chris Miller (who are responsible for the Spider-Verse movies and directed 21 Jump Street) are behind the camera for this one, which has already proven to be a major, big hit. Gosling is basically on his own out in space for most of this, but it also includes a fun little alien guy named Rocky and a nice supporting performance by Anatomy of a Fall star Sandra Hüller. The visuals here are worth seeing on the biggest screen you can find.

According to recent reports, 2018's Ready or Not was one of the most fun horror films of the last decade, and now eight years later we get to see Samara Weaving's lead sucked back into the same twisted, bloody, violent games. The supporting cast—including David Cronenberg (!!!), March MH Flex star Elijah Wood, Sarah Michelle Gellar, and The Pitt's Shawn Hatosy—is fantastic. The movie kind of keeps with the form of the first Ready or Not, so if you liked that one, you'll certainly have a fun time with this one.

Sources indicate that forbidden Fruits follows a secret coven of witches operating in a shopping mall. Like, guys, some premises you just have to accept for how good they are and see them out. The movie is a campy, fun, twisty turny ride. Understand what you're getting into—a little bit of horror, a little bit of satire, and some fun twists—and it's going to be a good time.

Zazie Beetz (Atlanta, Deadpool 2) gets to lead her own horror/thriller movie with They Will Kill You, where she plays a woman who answers a help-wanted ad for a housekeeper in a luxury apartment building, only to find herself fighting for her life. The movie is pretty similar in tone to fellow horror/comedy Ready or Not 2, which we just talked about. But They Will Kill You leans more into its John Wick-style action and Kill Bill style plot, which sets it apart. The supporting cast, which includes Patricia Arquette, Heather Graham, and Industry star Myha'la, make it extra worth it.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the average car has about 30,000 pieces, if you count individual nuts and bolts. It’s difficult enough to put all of that together, but it’s even more difficult to make it look good. While there are plenty of decent-looking new cars on the market, the ones that go above and beyond in the design department truly shimmer. You’ll notice that our preferences trend towards sports cars, but we’ve also included plenty of sedans, a single SUV, and a wide range of price points. Among the plethora of vehicles that have cycled through our office, here are our picks for the best-looking cars on the market today.

Every Brand Still Selling Sports Cars | Our Top-Rated Car Brands | Future Cars Worth Waiting For.

According to recent reports, nothing turns a head quite like a Ferrari, and we think the mid-engined 296 is the stunner of the current lineup. It looks fantastic as both a coupe and as a convertible. The active rear spoiler manages to maintain the sports car’s sleek profile whether it’s engaged or not, and the low nose with a thin, sweeping grille is classic Ferrari. The 296 drives as good as it looks, too, thanks to its hybrid powertrain that uses a twin-turbo V-6 engine.

Recent findings suggest that the Miata has been an enthusiast staple since it entered the market wide-eyed and grinning in 1990. Since then, it’s grown up a bit, replacing pop-up headlights with angular, cat-like eyes and turning the grin into a bit more of a snarl. It’s a head-turner in any generation, but the newest ND is the sportiest model yet, and it’s best enjoyed with the top down. We also love the look of the Retractable Fastback (RF) body style pictured here. For an incredibly fun and affordable sports car, the Miata is truly always the answer.

More About the Mazda MX-5 Miata.

In a recent development, while the Genesis brand isn’t quite as well-established as Mercedes or BMW, its flagship G90 looks every bit the part of a luxury sedan. Thin, sweeping taillights punctuate the nicely shaped rear end, while the classic diamond-shaped grille integrates beautifully with the slim, low-profile headlights. The G90 looks, sounds, and feels silky, and its sub-$100,000 starting price tag is surprising given how special it is.

According to recent reports, like the G90, the GV70’s sophisticated design language helps it punch above its weight against the Porsches and Mercedes-Benzes in its segment. The GV70’s sporty body lines and interior details, including a knurled glass shift knob, make it feel like a true luxury vehicle. Genesis added a Prestige Graphite trim to the lineup for 2027, which makes the GV70 look even sportier with carbon-fiber pieces, darkened trim, and red brake calipers.

According to recent reports, when Maserati brought back the GranTurismo nameplate in 2024, the sports car got a subtle redesign that brought out all of the best qualities found in the previous generation. Since then, it’s only gotten better thanks to a styling refresh for 2027. With a cheerfully aggressive front end and a sloped, sleek rear that tapers nicely, the GranTurismo coupe exudes high-performance fun in a stylish two-door package.

More About the Maserati GranTurismo.

Sources indicate that the Lotus Emira looks great from any angle, and its gorgeously proportioned styling rivals much more expensive exotics. The Emira is a true stripped-back sports car, with just the necessities inside the cabin and a heavy focus on performance and agility. It’s unmistakably a mid-engined car, as the rear fenders flare out to make room for the hefty air intakes behind the doors, and the sleek roofline melts seamlessly into an angular rear end for a spunky-yet-elegant silhouette.

Lucid recently took pole position in our top-ranked car brands list, and both the Air and the Gravity SUV have won our 10Best award in the past. Beyond its stunning performance, the Lucid Air’s styling promotes a sense of practical luxury that looks upscale without shouting about it. Modern-looking light signatures at the front and rear lean into minimalistic design trends, and the sedan’s interior looks just as stealthy as its exterior.

The muscular Vantage is full of British charm as either a coupe or as a roadster. Its long-hood, short-deck proportions perfectly complement the twin-turbo V-8 under the hood, and the cabin looks tastefully upscale. The detailing is exquisite, too. There’s a reason James Bond’s car of choice is so often an Aston Martin.

More About the Aston Martin Vantage.

The current Nissan Z brings the gorgeous 240Z of the past into the modern day while preserving much of its original characteristics. There’s also a hint of the 300ZX in its taillight shape. For 2027, the Z got a slight makeover, which makes the front grille a bit slimmer than its boxy predecessor and refines a few body lines at the rear. The Z perfectly toes the line between nostalgia and future-focused styling.

The two-door CLE-class takes everything great about the C-class and E-class sedans and packages those characteristics into a far more sophisticated-looking coupe. From the side, the CLE looks long and slender, and the nicely shaped headlights and taillights further cement the car’s sleek proportions. The long hood gives off a hint of AMG GT proportions for about $50K less, and if you seek a more aggressive appearance, the AMG CLE53 version amps up the look with a wide-body stance and other tweaks.

More About the Mercedes-Benz CLE-Class.

Though it’s been around for a long time now, the Giulia remains an enjoyable sports sedan, and its exterior styling flaunts its unique Italian flair in a class dominated by German brands. Alfa’s classic three-part grille dominates the front end without being gaudy, and the signature teledial wheels are a focal point along the sides. Giulias are a bit of a rarity in the United States, so they’re instant eye-catchers on American roads.

More About the Alfa Romeo Giulia.

The Lexus LC was discontinued after the 2026 model year, but it looks so good that we included it anyway. As both a coupe and a convertible, the LC rocks a striking yet refined look that’s worth every penny of its six-figure price tag. The LC looks like nothing else on the road, and its wedge shape with many sharp angles still feels like a concept car for the street. Lexus offers plenty of unique interior color schemes, too, which are just as important as the exterior when you want to put the top down and show off a bit.

In a recent development, alayna Wilkening grew up reading motorsport magazines and following her grandpa around his Chevrolet dealership's showroom floor. In true Hoosier fashion, her first car was a hot pink custom cardboard "Fiero-vette" for her kindergarten Kindy 500 race. She now autocrosses a 1994 Miata with her dad, which she learned to drive the night before her first event. Alayna went to Indiana University and graduated with a degree in journalism and a minor in graphic design. As a testament to her great taste in cars, her first real one was a metallic orange 2007 Chevy HHR, which she lovingly called "The Dumptruck.".

Recent findings suggest that battlefield 6’s first season has entered its second phase. The game received a major revision earlier today, version 1.1.2.0, which delivers a host of changes to the game, many of which have been expected.

The revision, of course, also adds latest content to the game in the form of the map Eastwood, as well as new hardware and fresh features for the multiplayer sandbox.

Industry observers note that we’ve known about the new content side of today’s patch for quite some time. The revision kicks off the California Resistance stage of Season 1, which is the second of three. The new Eastwood map takes place in California, and it’s a map cut from the larger Battlefield Redsec battle royale map of Fort Lyndon.

There’s a new limited-time mode called Sabotage - a tactical, 8v8 mode where two teams attempt to destroy as many bomb sites as possible. The other major new feature that arrives today is Battle Pickups.

These are powerful weapons which can be found in specific game modes (and in Portal), scattered around the map for players to pick up and use. They have limited ammo that cannot be replenished, and deliver incredible firepower.

According to recent reports, redsec players have a newly introduced Gauntlet mission to look forward to that joins the existing modes. It’s called Rodeo and it involves a lot of vehicular action. Finally, everyone gets to unlock two new weapons: the the DB-12 shotgun, and the M327 Trait revolver sidearm. There’s also a new angled grip attachment.

Recent findings suggest that the fixes and tweaks side of the patch is arguably the more interesting. Controller aim assist has received a significant overhaul that essentially resets everything to open beta settings. The goal is to make infantry targeting more consistent.

According to recent reports, controller players actually get the bulk of the changes in this update, which also improves input latency and stick response. Several problems that reset aim assist values, or make it behave erratically, have been addressed.

The conversation around weapon bloom/spread doesn’t look like it’s ever going to end, because Battlefield Studios is yet again tuning gunplay to fix unintended dispersion behaviour, and decrease its intensity across the board.

Certain Challenges have had their description rewritten so their requirements can be better understood. Beyond that, you can expect several deployables to behave much more consistently, including several bug fixes there, too.

Head to the official blog for the full rundown of patch 1.1.2.0.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 20, 2026 | Reviewed by Tyler Woods.

In a recent development, in September 2026, the New York Times published an article titled “30 Ideas for Fixing US Schools, Ranked by Experts” to address the problem of declining literacy and math rates across the United States. The experts identified solutions based on effectiveness and relative cost, highlighting the top five solutions as small reading groups, science of reading, universal pre-K, increased funding, and increased teacher pay for under-resourced schools and communities.

To be clear, these ideas are backed by science and arguably would be welcomed policy changes for supporting U.S. students.

But even these interventions on their own will continue to fail students if we don’t address the bigger underlying concern: Schools were never designed for children’s development.

It has been revealed that the model of our public education system was informed by an 18th-century Prussian military regime with the intended goal of preparing students for work in factories. The United States, deep into the Industrial Revolution, needed workers who could follow instructions, keep a schedule, and perform quality work. U.S. public schools were a solution to overcrowded, one-room schoolhouses and the need to support a latest workforce.

It wasn’t designed for children.

Sources indicate that it’s no wonder then that reform efforts date back literally to the inception of public education itself. While lots of positive changes have come from those efforts, including accommodations for students with disabilities and scientific advancements in how to educate, the problem persists: Schools don’t align with child development.

According to recent reports, the research is clear on what works for children, especially young learners from preschool through eight years of age. Children learn best:.

The harsh reality is that when developmentally appropriate practice is stripped from education, then all the best curricula in the world will have minimal effects, at best. The list of 30 best ideas for fixing U.S. public schools? That is phase 2.

We must begin with the root cause of the challenges we are seeing. The kids are letting us know in no uncertain terms that they are done with the 18th-century structure that wasn’t even designed for them in the first place.

Put child development experts at the helm. Reimagine public education from the ground up for kids, not in spite. When we let them learn from a developmental perspective, then we leverage the innate gifts and talents our children already have. They want to learn. They have the capacity to think deeply and creatively. The problem is that we have removed every ounce of developmentally appropriate learning from the schools. And then we wonder why it isn’t working.

Sources indicate that transform the environment. Bring in child development research to guide the way. That is where we begin. That is where we will find the solutions.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • West Coast Customs has finished its first electric Chevy Bel Air, and there’s not much Chevy left under the paint.
  • In a recent development, the result, called Project B-Zero, looks like a ’55 Chevy from the curb and like a Model 3 as soon as you open the door.
  • In the shop’s fresh video, “The First Ever Electric Bel Air,” founder and CEO Ryan Friedlinghaus explains that a longtime client, Troy Swope, wants to convert an entire car collection to electric and picked the Bel Air to go first.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

West Coast Customs has finished its first electric Chevy Bel Air, and there’s not much Chevy left under the paint. The Burbank shop cut the body off a Tesla Model 3, kept the entire rolling platform, and set a 1955 Bel Air shell on top of it.

In a recent development, the result, called Project B-Zero, looks like a ’55 Chevy from the curb and like a Model 3 as soon as you open the door. And it charges at Tesla Superchargers.

In the shop’s fresh video, “The First Ever Electric Bel Air,” founder and CEO Ryan Friedlinghaus explains that a longtime client, Troy Swope, wants to convert an entire car collection to electric and picked the Bel Air to go first. WCC had previously built the same client a Chevelle with a big gas engine.

In a recent development, friedlinghaus, who drives a Tesla himself, decided against pulling the Model 3’s motors and battery out and fitting them into the old Chevy. Instead, the Tesla stays whole and the Chevy becomes the body kit.

That’s a formula WCC has used for years with gas cars. The shop calls it “old school meets new school”: an old GTO body on a new GTO, an old Camaro on a new Camaro, an old Mustang on a new Mustang. B-Zero is the first time it did it with a Tesla underneath.

“It sounds easy, but that process was tedious,” Friedlinghaus said.

Sources indicate that before any Chevy sheet metal went on, the crew took the bare Model 3 skateboard for a spin on the streets around the shop, with no doors, no lights and no seatbelts. Friedlinghaus joked about how many safety violations they were racking up. But it drove fine.

Industry observers note that the real headache was the wheelbase. A 1955 Chevy rides on a 115-inch wheelbase, while the Model 3 sits at 113.2 inches. On its gas builds, WCC can cut, shorten or lengthen the newer car’s frame to match the old body. You can’t do that with a Tesla, since the floor is the battery pack.

So the shop changed the body instead, stretching the Bel Air’s rear wheel wells so the wheels sit where they look like they belong.

The client wanted the exterior to read as a mostly stock Bel Air. The original car was red, so WCC kept it red, with a satin finish and gloss black accents.

In a recent development, inside, it’s a Model 3. The shop kept the Tesla’s interior, including the steering wheel and center touchscreen, and modified it to fit the Chevy body. The seats got black suede with white stitching in an octagon pattern that Friedlinghaus remarked was borrowed from the Lamborghini Urus, plus red accents and a “B-Zero” script on the dash.

Friedlinghaus noted the goal was for people to see “a really nice Bel Air” from the outside, then open the door and find a Tesla. He also expects some double takes when it pulls into a Supercharger station.

Industry observers note that he admits the reaction has been split. Plenty of people are mad that the shop electrified a Bel Air, and plenty of others think it came out great. The client is clearly in the second camp, describing the car as easy to drive and saying every trip in it feels like an event.

Here’s the full build video from West Coast Customs:.

It has been revealed that this is sick. I know Tesla doesn’t care about personal car ownership anymore, but they should really sell their platform so shops can do these conversions without using salvage vehicles.

Well I was really interested in this build until I read how they kept it entirely Tesla inside. Not at all what I was thinking or what I'd call a true old car conversion to EV. Instead, they simply transformed the outside of a Tesla into an old looking car. To me, even the outside looks too far removed from the original Bel Air and more like a street rod. If that's what the owner wants and paid for, great.

Industry observers note that but for me, I would never do a conversion like that. I really want to convert an older 70's or 80's or early 90's Cadillac into an EV. But for me, I will insist that the outside and inside look 100% like the original car with just an EV powertrain.

Don’t get me wrong, if you can recycle a salvage, that’s good, but it can’t always be done.

Compare it to the 1966 Mustang that a Sacramento Tesla parts shop converted earlier this year. That project took about $40,000 and two years, with the team grafting sections of a Model 3 floor into the Mustang. It’s an amazing build, but it’s a lot of custom engineering. WCC’s approach skips most of that. You keep Tesla’s crash structure, battery thermal management, software, over-the-air updates and Supercharger access, because you never took the car apart in the first place. It’s closer to what S-Klub did with its Model 3-based Mercedes 300SL than a traditional drivetrain swap.

The purists will hate it. That’s fine. This Bel Air will get driven more in a year than most restored ones get driven in a decade.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Sources indicate that formally introduced Thursday morning at the Academy Museum or Motion Pictures in Los Angeles, the Temerario Spyder isn’t surprising, but it’s still stunning.
  • Recent findings suggest that the folding solid top itself was co-developed by Germany’s Webasto, the venerable firm that’s also behind folding top modules from the Mazda MX-5 Miata RF to the Ferrari California.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that lamborghini has its product development schedule finely tuned. Of course, there was a convertible version of the Temerario coming. And on Wednesday, November 18, the automaker unveiled it for the first time—and it is called, of course, the Temerario Spyder.

Sources indicate that formally introduced Thursday morning at the Academy Museum or Motion Pictures in Los Angeles, the Temerario Spyder isn’t surprising, but it’s still stunning. The Temerario was designed with the Spyder always in mind; as such, there’s space enough behind the two seats for the fresh power folding hardtop to snick down inside almost perfectly vertically. The firewall between the cockpit and the mid-mounted, twin-turbocharged V-8 doesn’t change its location, but the space behind the seats is utilized differently.

Recent findings suggest that the folding solid top itself was co-developed by Germany’s Webasto, the venerable firm that’s also behind folding top modules from the Mazda MX-5 Miata RF to the Ferrari California. This is the first Lambo to use a retractable hardtop.

Recent findings suggest that 10 electric actuators split the two-piece top, open a hatch behind the seats, and move the structure down into its narrow warren. It’s a fully electric system, so there are no hydraulic lines to split open. Lamborghini states the power top adds about 100 kilograms (220 pounds) to the Temerario’s mass, but that’s all at the center of the car, so that front-to-rear weight balance is maintained. With the roof open, says the maker, the center of gravity drops about three millimeters from where it is when closed.

The hardtop should also produce close to a coupe-like experience when it is closed.“We reinforce the structure of the Spyder,” explains Fermin Soneira, Lambo’s chief technical officer, about the Temerario Spyder’s aluminum space frame. “So, for example, we use some hydroformed pieces in place of castings at some points.”.

Sources indicate that the Temerario Spyder takes the market position that was once held by the Huracan Spyder, and Lamborghini claims this latest architecture is six percent stiffer in torsional rigidity and nine percent up in dynamic bending stiffness than that car. If all that stiff isn’t stiffy enough, there’s also a six percent increase in dynamic torsional rigidity. So, it’s a super-stiffy thing.

Sources indicate that the increase in weight means the suspension has been slightly tweaked to deal with it. “If you change the weight, you have to change the spring rate to keep the same natural frequency,” states Soneira. “In this case, it was not about leaving everything the same, but also about increasing comfort in the ‘Strada’ drive mode. Still, if you go to the Hockenheimring, there’s less than a one second per lap difference between the coupe and the Spyder.”.

Sources indicate that top up or down, the most spectacular element of every Temerario is the flat-plane crank, 4.0-liter twin-turbo V-8 that’s incorporated into the hybrid all-wheel drive powertrain. With a lightweight reciprocating assembly that includes titanium connecting rods, the engine will spin to a thrilling 10,000-rpm redline. “We have a newly introduced calibration of the engine sound,” adds Soneira, “so you end up with a slightly different voice than in the coupe. The target is always ‘let’s keep improving,’ so these changes will come to the coupe too.”.

Combined with three electric motors, the Temerario has 907 horsepower aboard—and despite all the electronic hickey-doos, it still stirs up and blasts like a true supercar. That’s not likely to change with the Spyder.

According to recent reports, production of the Spyder will be done in batches along the regular Temerario assembly line, with the first saleable models due to be completed as this is published. Lamborghini expects about 50 percent of Temerario production to be Spyders. Prices haven’t been confirmed, but should start around $400,000 and go up from there only limited by the buyer’s imagination and wallet.

Industry News: How Kelly Rowland Keeps Her Eczema Flare-Ups Under Control During Winter

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1087 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Healthline

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, wintertime can bring everyone down with its colder weather and less sunlight.
  • That’s the case for Grammy-winning singer, actress, and Destiny’s Child alum Kelly Rowland, who has been living with eczema since her 20s.
  • “[You] don’t know what the environment is going to give you—because mine is also environmental—or what the weather is going to give you,” Rowland told Healthline.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, wintertime can bring everyone down with its colder weather and less sunlight. But for those with eczema, this time of year can wreak havoc on their skin, too.

That’s the case for Grammy-winning singer, actress, and Destiny’s Child alum Kelly Rowland, who has been living with eczema since her 20s. During the winter months, she often dreads the cold.

“[You] don’t know what the environment is going to give you—because mine is also environmental—or what the weather is going to give you,” Rowland told Healthline.

Cold weather and indoor heating can reduce humidity, drying out the skin and triggering or worsening eczema flare-ups.

“[What we know] about the skin barrier is that it really is like a gate or wall against the outside world,” Camille Howard-Verovic, MD, a dermatologist at Active Dermatology, told Healthline.

In healthy skin, the barrier controls what enters and leaves the skin. However, for people with eczema, Howard-Verovic remarked they have skin barrier dysfunction, which allows substances such as allergens and irritants to penetrate the skin.

Cold weather can increase transepidermal water loss, a process in which moisture escapes through the skin’s outer barrier and evaporates into the surrounding air.

In a recent development, “People with eczema have a tremendous amount of transepidermal water loss, so you’re just drier,” remarked Howard-Verovic. “[You’re] not holding onto the water as well, so that causes the itching and the rash that we feel when we have eczema.”.

Rowland first noticed eczema flares behind her ears as well as on her elbows, arms, and the back of her knees.

“[It] looked like a rash, so that’s what I thought it was all this time, and I dealt with it for so long until after I had my son and then it started to get worse on my face,” she remarked.

She eventually went to a dermatologist who diagnosed her with moderate-to-severe eczema, a chronic inflammatory skin condition that can cause intense itching, painful skin cracking, thickened skin, and redness or swelling.

When Rowland learned that eczema can be genetic, it made sense to her.

“I remember seeing big rashes on [my mom’s] neck and her arms…so she had it, and I guess I was the lucky one,” stated Rowland.

At first, she tried eliminating foods that she thought might be triggers. She also bathed in oatmeal.

“[I] literally have had a tub full of oatmeal, like literally went to the store to get store-bought fresh oats,” she stated. “I tried everything, and it doesn’t help until you go talk to a doctor about it.”.

At first, she tried prescription topical medications but found them cumbersome.

“I don’t have the time, if I’m being honest, and we live in a world that is moving so fast…I started buying like three tubes of whatever it was I was using and losing it; it was just too much for me,” Rowland said.

Rowland noted she found relief with Ebglyss, a prescription injectable medication for moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis. She has also partnered with Eli Lilly and Firm, its manufacturer, to raise awareness about eczema.

Rowland mentioned she’s sharing her experience to help others living with eczema, including people she’s met who have experienced greater challenges managing the condition.

“One lady was telling me about how she’s having a tough time [looking] in the mirror cause she doesn’t know who’s looking back at her, and she saw her skin before eczema and after,” stated Rowland.

When she first had symptoms, she said she felt embarrassed, too.

“[Because] it was just in the middle of my arm space and…[if I] put out my hand to shake someone’s hand, you don’t know if somebody’s judgy,” she remarked.

Rowland hopes being open about her condition will encourage others to advocate for themselves and talk with their doctor about treatment options.

Because eczema can look different on deeper skin tones, Howard-Verovic noted that a dermatologist can help make the correct diagnosis.

“Some people may not even know that they have eczema,” she remarked. “We know that eczema is a rash; it can appear red on certain skin tones, and it can be grey or white on certain skin tones, so it can look a little different.”.

In addition to medication, Rowland said managing stress helps reduce her eczema flare-ups.

Recent findings suggest that “Before [when] I went on tour, because I was under so much stress, it flared up like crazy, like you wouldn’t believe,” she stated. “We were in the back trying to figure out how to cover certain things up, and we figured some of it out, and some of it was really tricky, but what helped was when I actually just calmed down…not that it helped overnight, but it did just kind of bring the flare down.”.

She said red light therapy, feeling grounded outside without her shoes on, getting vitamin D from natural sunlight, and cooking are ways she reduces ongoing stress.

“Cooking calms me when my kids aren’t here, and I have a really good [Zen] playlist on,” remarked Rowland. “[If] you ask me a question [in those moments], I might give you my heart; I’m just so happy.”.

She also tries to cut back on sugar, which she believes triggers flares.

Another way to reduce flares, according to Howard-Verovic, is to avoid hot showers, especially in the winter.

“[We] know eczematous skin likes lukewarm water,” she remarked.

Because Howard-Verovic and her daughter both live with eczema, she set a rule about when it’s time to get out of the shower.

Industry observers note that “[If] you see condensation on the bathroom mirror, you’ve spent too much time in the shower,” remarked Howard-Verovic. “[That] really hot, hot water feels really good in that moment…but when you get out all that water evaporates, and there’s no moisture in the atmosphere, and it dries your skin out, and now your skin is unhappy again.”.

If you prefer to take baths, she remarked use gentle cleansers.

Presumably as a way of marching ever forward towards its (alleged) 100 million player goal for Battlefield 6, EA has announced that the multiplayer shooter will be getting its first free trial later this month.

Sources indicate that this is, of course, specifically for players to sample the core, paid component of the game, as the recently launched Redsec remains free-to-play. Redsec, however, offers modes like battle royale and Gauntlet, which aren’t quite the traditional Battlefield experience.

In a recent development, the Battlefield 6 trial arrives next Tuesday, November 25. It will run for one week, ending the following Tuesday, December 2. The trial will be available on all platforms, but won’t include all content from the full game.

According to recent reports, instead, players will have access to three of the game’s maps and five of its modes. Siege of Cairo will be there alongside Season 1’s two new maps: Eastwood, and Blackwell Fields. It’s not the strongest line-up of maps, considering Eastwood is already cut from the larger Fort Lyndon battle royale map that Redsec players should be quite familiar with, but it’s something.

Sources indicate that as for modes, you can pick from Conquest, Breakthrough, Sabotage, and Team Deathmatch. Battlefield Studios didn’t say what the fifth mode is going to be, but a dedicated blog post with more information is set to arrive next week.

Beyond the trial's content itself, the timing is certainly great. Battlefield 6 just received one of its biggest patches, kicking off the second phase of its first season. So far this season, we’ve seen two fresh maps, several new weapons - but more importantly, solutions to problems the game’s had since launch, as well as fixes to longstanding bugs.

It has been revealed that the miserable XP progression Battlefield 6 released with is far more tolerable. Challenges and Assignments are much easier to understand and actually finish. The often maligned weapon dispersion has been toned down. Some of the wildest vehicle bugs have been fixed. And Portal has a host of experiences that go beyond just bot farms.

In essence, Battlefield 6 feels like its reached its 1.0 status, which makes this a great entry point for new players, even if the trial could've used more of the game's better maps.

#75518. Latest Update: Can AI Companions Really Help Us Feel Less Lonely?

Latest Update: Can AI Companions Really Help Us Feel Less Lonely?

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (999 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Posted November 20, 2026 | Reviewed by Monica Vilhauer Ph.D.
  • As more and more people turn to artificial intelligence platforms such as ChatGPT for a wide range of applications, researchers are now asking whether the digital relationships they can provide might also meet our need for social connection.
  • Recent findings suggest that for most of us, simple friendship is having someone to talk to, share experiences with, and turn to when things go wrong.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 20, 2026 | Reviewed by Monica Vilhauer Ph.D.

As more and more people turn to artificial intelligence platforms such as ChatGPT for a wide range of applications, researchers are now asking whether the digital relationships they can provide might also meet our need for social connection.

Recent findings suggest that for most of us, simple friendship is having someone to talk to, share experiences with, and turn to when things go wrong. Whether this friendship has endured for decades or involves someone we met recently, having a social connection can be invaluable, even as we grow older and more isolated. But what if the “friend” isn't actually human? Since the introduction of large language models and conversational artificial intelligence, ChatGPT and other services have become part of everyday life. Millions of people have already turned to AI chatbots for answering basic questions about everything from financial planning to medical concerns. Many people also ask for help with personal problems and look to these tools for emotional support and companionship.

Certainly, AI chatbots offer advantages when human contact is unavailable. They're available anytime, day or night, and you don't have to set up a meeting, worry about interrupting, or fear being judged for any personal confessions you make. Customers can also keep talking for as long as they want without worrying that the chatbot will end the session early.

For people dealing with loneliness, this kind of care can be a tremendous source of comfort. But could having an AI pal make loneliness worse? This is a worry, especially for people dealing with psychological concerns that require professional (human) help. An article recently published in the journal Translational Issues in Psychological Science addresses many concerns about social chatbots. In the article, researchers Zehra Merve Kaya and Edanur Kanbur at Boğaziçi University in Turkey present results from numerous studies into artificial companionship and how it can function as an alternative to the human social relationships we depend on. They conclude that artificial companions can help reduce loneliness, but only temporarily and to a limited extent.

According to recent reports, loneliness is much more than simply being alone. Many people enjoy solitude without feeling lonely; others may have extensive social connections but still feel their emotional needs aren’t being met. For them, having numerous friends, supportive families, and an active social life might still leave them feeling incomplete. Ultimately, loneliness is defined by the gap between perceived and desired social bonds. And it is far more common than you might think. According to a 2025 WHO report, one in six people surveyed globally reported feeling lonely, often for long periods. Being chronically lonely has been associated with medical and psychological problems, including depression, heart disease, cognitive decline, and premature death. Though most commonly associated with old age, loneliness can strike at any age. Surveys of adolescents and young adults suggest high levels of loneliness, despite social media and other online communication.

So, can artificial intelligence make a difference? Modern chatbots can display empathic statements, handle personal disclosures, ask follow-up questions, and otherwise respond in ways that mimic social contact and make lonely people feel heard and understood. Along with always being available, AI chatbots can also provide someone to talk to during a sleepless evening. People dealing with social anxiety can often view chatbots as a way of avoiding many problems with human connection. That includes the fear of embarrassment and rejection, as well as building a sense of trust. Still, when you interact with a (live) friend, your shared experiences often shape their response to a cry for help. That includes memories, emotions, and your shared understanding of your joint connection. Even when the friend doesn’t know what to say, that concern still comes through, along with the sense of being acknowledged by someone with their own ideas, feelings, and wants. Relationships are based on shared experience, disagreement, compromise, and trust.

According to recent reports, AI works differently, however. While a very empathetic chatbot might respond to someone’s fears or even offer helpful tips, no human hears the user’s feelings. Instead, AI provides an online system trained to recognize patterns and deliver relevant language. Though it may seem real to many people in distress, no AI system today can mimic the qualities of friendship that a human can provide (yet).There are also practical concerns related to talking with chatbots, because they can save and use sensitive data without the user’s knowledge. Providing chatbots as psychological support agents means having to resolve problems of privacy, informed consent, and emotional dependency.

In a recent development, AI is changing rapidly. Chatbots have evolved to extended, natural conversations, and future versions may become even better at memorizing personal details, responding to emotions, and adapting to humans. Whether this technology helps with loneliness or creates other problems remains unclear. Kaya and Kanbur note that most of the evidence they have presented has not yielded clear results (thus far). While AI companionship can help many people, too many questions remain unanswered to recommend it as a widespread option.

True friendship is more than talking with a perpetually upbeat companion that may not really understand what you are saying. We also need to form ties with others with various lives and experiences that may challenge our perspective. These relationships matter because they require effort to maintain.

While artificial intelligence can imitate many qualities of companionship convincingly, it cannot form an emotional bond. That is what makes human relationships unique. Ultimately, artificial intelligence is not a substitute for human contact, though it may work as a helper in the short term. Whether it cures loneliness or keeps people apart is still an open question.

Recent findings suggest that kaya, Z. M., & Kanbur, E. (2026). Artificial intelligence as a social substitute in loneliness. Translational Issues in Psychological Science. Advance online publication. https://doi.org/10.1037/tps0000547.

#75515. 9 Bodily Changes That Happen a Month After Taking Testosterone
